sections.heading: 4. Rehearse the entire workflow before accepting live commitments
paragraphs: Run a production rehearsal using a public solicitation that matches the desk's intended niche. Download its attachments, establish the current amendment set, identify mandatory experience and certifications, and assign a primary owner plus a backup reviewer. Reconstruct the deadline from the source document, including time zone and submission channel. Prepare a compliance matrix linking each requirement to its proposed response location and responsible client subject-matter owner. The desk must distinguish an absent requirement from evidence it has not yet received. Review pricing units for each line item; a monthly service priced as an annual quantity can destroy otherwise sound economics. Have someone outside the drafting workflow verify the final attachment names, signature authority, required representations, and acknowledgment of amendments. Rehearse uploads only in a permitted practice environment or local simulation; do not submit a live bid as a test. Save the checklist, timing log, and defects in a reusable job folder. Launch only after the team can reproduce the workflow without relying on an individual's inbox or memory. Where the agency offers no practice portal, document submission instructions and plan an early real upload with the client's authorization.

Test money movement separately from proposal production. The person changing vendor bank details should not be the sole approver of the first payment to that account. Confirm changes through a previously established telephone number, not contact information supplied in the change email. Use bank dual authorization where available; a solo operator should document independent client or bookkeeper verification for material changes. Never route client purchase funds or tax-credit principal through the ordinary operating account merely to simplify reporting. A qualified escrow provider should define release conditions, account ownership, dispute handling, and callback procedures in signed instructions. Reconcile each service invoice to the engagement, delivery acceptance, and ledger entry. For federal payments, inspect the actual payment clause and invoice submission system; 31 U.S.C. 3902 does not turn an incomplete or disputed invoice into immediately available cash. The forecast should survive a sixty-day collection delay and the loss of the largest unsigned opportunity. Simulate a supplier missing a delivery milestone, then identify contractual substitution rights and a qualified backup. If replacement costs consume the entire service fee, reject or reprice the scope before promising a delivery date the supplier cannot substantiate.

Measure readiness with evidence, then expand only the constraint that actually limits earned fees. The launch packet should contain the reserve reconciliation, signed scope template, current policy documents, access register, tested recovery record, rehearsal results, and an example accepted invoice. Weekly reporting should show qualified opportunities, paid engagements, delivery hours, amendment defects, invoice aging, and cash coverage. Do not reward the team for gross bid volume when most opportunities fail eligibility or capacity checks. A useful capacity threshold is booked delivery hours divided by available paid hours for the next four weeks; investigate before that ratio exceeds 80%, leaving room for amendments and rework. At twenty additional hours required, a $65 hourly specialist costs $1,300; approve that expense only against priced scope and sufficient collection coverage. Preserve the canonical cases when reporting progress: $120,000 at 15% yields $18,000; $560,000 at 22.5% yields $126,000; $1,000,000 at 30% yields $300,000. Those are annual scenario outputs, not monthly run rates or promised outcomes. Maintain separate dashboards for client award value, credit principal, recognized service revenue, contribution after direct work, and owner profit. That separation keeps impressive transaction volume from concealing an underfunded service business.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #4, Government Contract Brokering, ranks #27 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: a High-Leverage Operator Play, not effortless procurement arbitrage. Seven chapter-mapped plays anchor this teardown: federal bid-desk retainers, municipal solicitation monitoring, prime/sub teaming support, fixed-fee proposal production, subcontract administration, invoice-evidence operations, and white-label MVNO/Lifeline aggregation. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $18,000 Conservative, $126,000 Base, and $300,000 Scaled, against recognized service revenue of $120,000, $560,000, and $1,000,000. Award face values and carrier subsidies do not become broker revenue. The chapter converts common failure mechanisms into evidence tests, loss limits, and stop-work triggers. The question's 80% framing is not an observed failure rate; the operating controls stand without that unsupported statistic.

sections.heading: 1. Separate Paid Procurement Work from Influence Selling
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is selling access instead of a measurable service. A federal bid desk can research public solicitations, maintain calendars, draft responses, and document supplier qualifications; it cannot promise an award through personal influence. FAR Subpart 3.4 and the solicitation's applicable FAR 52.203-5 clause govern contingent-fee arrangements, including the bona fide employee or agency exception. Do not assume that calling a percentage payment consulting makes the exception available. A prohibited arrangement can expose the contractor to annulment or recovery of the fee. The second trap is treating a teaming introduction as an unrestricted referral business: 41 U.S.C. chapter 87 addresses kickbacks connected with federal prime contracts and subcontracts. The third is accepting nonpublic competitor pricing or source-selection material; 41 U.S.C. 2102 reaches prohibited disclosure and knowing receipt before award. Require a written scope, a documented fee rationale, and a source log for every sensitive attachment. Quarantine unsolicited restricted material, stop its circulation, preserve the message, and route it to designated counsel and the responsible contracting channel. Never delete evidence to make a bid file look clean.

Map the first four operating plays to delivered units, not award percentages. Federal bid-desk retainers might charge $1,500 monthly for twelve staff hours at $60 plus $180 of allocated tooling, leaving $600 contribution before central overhead. Municipal solicitation monitoring might charge $600 for four hours at $60 plus $60 of portal and alert administration, leaving $300. Prime/sub teaming support might charge $2,000 for twenty hours at $60 plus $300 of documented diligence, leaving $500. Fixed-fee proposal production might charge $10,000 against $6,000 direct labor and $1,000 specialist review, leaving $3,000. These are illustrative service packages, not additional scorecard revenue or official catalog identifiers. The fallbacks are equally specific: cap monitored jurisdictions, require written client qualification before introductions, and reduce proposal scope when amendments expand the workload. Make payments depend on accepted deliverables rather than an award unless the actual arrangement has been reviewed under applicable restrictions. A fixed fee does not cure influence selling, kickbacks, organizational conflicts, or misuse of protected information. Price revision cycles and submission support explicitly; unlimited revisions quietly turn attractive contribution into unpaid overtime.

The fourth trap is impersonating the client in SAM.gov or a municipal portal. Use authorized roles, individual credentials, and multifactor authentication; never collect a principal's password to accelerate registration. SAM.gov registration and the Unique Entity ID are free, although a separately disclosed assistance service can carry a fee. The fifth trap is treating an active registration as proof of size, ownership, licensing, or performance capability. Verify the solicitation's actual representations and the responsible client's supporting records. The sixth is submitting through a borrowed identity after an access restriction. That can convert an administrative problem into a false representation or security incident. Record portal receipts, amendment acknowledgments, and the controlling deadline with its time zone. FAR 52.215-1 contains specific late-proposal rules when included; a successful upload to the wrong workspace does not establish timely receipt. Municipal procurement codes and portal instructions require separate review rather than automatic transplantation of FAR rules. Treat unexplained role changes, a rejected receipt, or one missing mandatory acknowledgment as a submission stop. Platform access restrictions and government suspension or debarment are different processes; neither should be described as an automatic permanent ban.

callout.title: Four Checks Before Any Client Submission
callout.body: Submission authority, fee structure, eligibility evidence, and receipt readiness must all be documented for the actual opportunity.
items: Match the client's authorized portal role to the person submitting; test multifactor access without sharing credentials.
Review the compensation agreement against FAR Subpart 3.4, applicable clauses, and jurisdiction-specific restrictions.
Obtain client-approved support for material representations, subcontract structure, and any claimed set-aside eligibility.
Rehearse the upload, confirm every amendment, and assign one person to capture the final timestamped receipt.

sections.heading: 2. Stop Pass-Through Structures and Supplier Defects Before They Become Debt
paragraphs: The seventh trap is building a nominal prime that contributes little beyond an invoice. FAR 52.215-23, when applicable, addresses excessive pass-through charges; its subcontracting threshold is a disclosure and analysis issue, not a universal ban on subcontracting. Separately, FAR 52.219-14 and 13 CFR 125.6 impose category-specific limitations on covered small business set-asides. For covered service contracts, the restriction generally limits payments to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities to 50% of the amount paid by the government, subject to the rule's details and exclusions. Supplies and construction have different tests. Do not substitute headcount, gross margin, or a teammate's marketing claim for the governing calculation. The eighth trap is ostensible-subcontractor affiliation under 13 CFR 121.103: an otherwise eligible small prime can lose eligibility through an impermissible reliance structure. Map primary and vital work, management control, relevant experience, and actual execution responsibilities before pricing. If the structure fails, move to a permissible support role or decline the opportunity. Adding a nominal project manager after submission does not retroactively repair inaccurate representations or an unsupported performance plan.

The ninth trap is quoting supplier promises as if they were binding capacity. A distributor's email is not a reserved production slot, an authorized substitution, or evidence of domestic-origin conformity. Build a requirement-to-evidence matrix covering delivery dates, inspection, packaging, origin clauses, cybersecurity terms, and required flowdowns. Buy American and trade-agreement clauses do not apply identically to every purchase; read the clauses actually incorporated. For a $200,000 client supply award, a $12,000 broker service fee remains $12,000 of potential operator revenue, not $200,000. If the operator guarantees supplier performance and must fund $20,000 of emergency replacement cost, the exposure exceeds that fee before ordinary labor costs. Do not accept that mismatch through casual indemnity language. Require verified lead times, inspection rights, written substitution procedures, and an allocated remedy for each material defect. A second qualified supplier is useful only when switching is contractually permitted and the replacement meets the same specifications. If neither condition holds, the fallback is to stop quoting the item and alert the prime, not quietly ship a near-match. Record supplier exceptions before the client commits.

The fifth mapped play, subcontract administration, can charge $1,000 monthly for eight hours at $60 plus $120 of document control, leaving $400 contribution before overhead. Its fallback is a capped exception queue and a written handoff to the prime for unresolved technical decisions. The sixth, invoice-evidence operations, can charge $500 per accepted invoice packet against four hours at $60 and $60 of review, leaving $200. Its fallback is paid remediation of missing acceptance records, not submission of unsupported quantities. The tenth trap is confusing administrative assistance with authority to certify delivery, change scope, or bind the government. Only appropriately authorized officials can make those commitments. FAR 32.905 links payment processing to a proper invoice and applicable acceptance requirements; an invoice number alone starts no reliable cash forecast. Track evidence from delivery through acceptance, invoice receipt, rejection, correction, and payment. A client contract should state whether the operator's service fee is independent of government collection. Pay-when-paid language transfers delay exposure to the desk; reject open-ended terms unless price, reserves, and enforceable remedies support the exposure. Never manufacture acceptance evidence to release a stuck receivable.

callout.title: Veteran Bid-Desk Tactics That Preserve Recoverable Margin
callout.body: Experienced desks price evidence work and isolate responsibilities before a delivery problem becomes an operator-funded rescue.
items: Ask the prime for its clause matrix before quoting administration; price mandatory reporting and flowdowns as explicit work units.
Compare the supplier's promised ship date with the required acceptance date, including transit, inspection, and correction time.
Keep separate folders for public solicitation research, client-controlled representations, and government acceptance evidence.
Maintain a qualified replacement supplier file, but confirm substitution authority before treating that supplier as usable backup.

sections.heading: 3. Treat Lifeline Aggregation as a Separate Recovery-Risk Business
paragraphs: The seventh mapped play is mvno_lifeline_acp_telecom_subsidy_aggregation: White-Label MVNO & Federal/State Low-Income Telecom Subsidy Aggregation. Its catalog identifier includes ACP, but ACP ended June 1, 2024; do not model new ACP reimbursements or sell ACP enrollment as a currently funded channel. Lifeline is a distinct program. Federal support can reach $9.25 monthly for qualifying service, with up to $25 additional support for eligible residents of qualifying Tribal lands, producing $34.25 before any separately validated state support. That is not a universal $44 household payment. California LifeLine has separate state requirements and support mechanics; never add headline benefits without checking the approved service, location, carrier status, and interaction rules. An MVNO arrangement does not itself confer Eligible Telecommunications Carrier status or authority to claim Lifeline support. Determine which ETC holds the obligation, which systems establish eligibility, and which entity submits reimbursement claims. The eleventh trap is buying enrollments before establishing that responsibility chain. A master aggregator earns its contracted service fee; carrier support receipts are not automatically the aggregator's recognized revenue. Obtain the executed carrier agreement before recruiting field agents.

The twelfth trap is selling hypothetical network economics as an unlimited-service entitlement. At 1,000 valid subscriber months, $9.25 support produces $9,250 of carrier support. Assumed $3 wholesale network cost produces $3,000 of network expense and a $6,250 spread before devices, support staff, taxes, eligibility work, usage costs, agent payments, recoveries, and carrier overhead. The $2–$4 wholesale range is an underwriting assumption requiring an actual tariff or contract; unlimited data promises may destroy it. An aggregator charging $2 per validated subscriber month records $2,000 of service revenue on those same units, not $9,250. If 100 units become ineligible for payment, reversing $200 of aggregator fees reduces recognized service revenue to $1,800; the ETC's associated $925 support adjustment is separate unless indemnity terms shift it. A $10,000 field campaign paying $10 for each of 1,000 activations takes five valid months of $2 fees merely to recover acquisition cash, ignoring all other costs and attrition. The fallback is a small verified cohort with capped acquisition exposure, payment holdbacks, and carrier reconciliation before national expansion. Do not fund hundreds of thousands of speculative activations.

The thirteenth trap is treating a submitted household record as durable eligibility. Apply 47 CFR 54.409, 54.410, 54.407, and 54.405 to eligibility, certification, support, and de-enrollment responsibilities. Use the National Verifier, National Lifeline Accountability Database, or applicable state process as required for the carrier and jurisdiction. Block duplicate households, fabricated documents, agent-controlled identities, and unsupported Tribal claims. These shortcuts can produce recoveries, termination, program exclusion, or false-claims exposure; fake traffic and forged usage records compound the harm. For service subject to the nonusage rules, deploy Day-20 SMS or IVR reminders, but distinguish reminders from qualifying usage. A subscriber's response to direct contact confirming continued service can qualify under the rule when properly captured; a delivered message alone does not. Follow the applicable 30-day nonusage and subsequent 15-day notice process rather than inventing immediate disconnection. Reverse field-agent commissions for lines failing the contractual 30-day usage test only through enforceable terms and applicable worker-payment rules. That commercial reversal does not replace the carrier's statutory process. Preserve consented contact records, actual usage evidence, exception decisions, and the linkage from subscriber month to claim.

sections.heading: 4. Reconcile the Scorecard and Install Cash-Loss Circuit Breakers
paragraphs: Use the canonical scorecard as the annual control total. Conservative recognized service revenue is $120,000, with $102,000 implied total costs and $18,000 owner net profit at 15%. Base is $560,000, $434,000 costs, and $126,000 profit at 22.5%. Scaled is $1,000,000, $700,000 costs, and $300,000 profit at 30%. Illustrative revenue bridges are ten $1,000 monthly retainers for Conservative; twenty $1,500 monthly retainers plus twenty $10,000 accepted projects for Base; and twenty-five $2,000 monthly retainers plus forty $10,000 accepted projects for Scaled. These bridges explain totals, not a promised customer mix or extra revenue layered onto the seven plays. The staffing labels remain 2 FT + 3 C for Conservative and Base, and 3 FT + 4 C for Scaled. Conservative costs leave little room for two full-time salaries, contractor purchases, and overhead; the scorecard alone does not establish a workable compensation plan. Build role-level hours and loaded rates before hiring. Do not silently treat unpaid owner labor as free capacity or move payroll outside the model to preserve its stated margin.

The fourteenth trap is confusing profitable bookings with spendable cash. Startup capital of $20,000–$90,000 and monthly operating expense of $5,000–$25,000 produce only one month of runway at the lowest-capital, highest-burn combination, versus thirty months at the opposite extremes, before setup spending or collections. First deals may take 3–12 months, so underwrite runway against a dated sales pipeline rather than the best endpoint. The monthly expense range is an operating planning input, not a substitute for total annual scorecard costs, which also must accommodate delivery labor and other attributable expense. Use a rolling thirteen-week cash forecast excluding restricted cash and disputed receipts. At Base, $434,000 annual costs average approximately $36,167 monthly. Ninety days of that full-cost run rate requires approximately $108,500 before incremental recovery exposure. A $24,000 unrecoverable defect cost reduces Base profit from $126,000 to $102,000 and margin to approximately 18.21%, assuming revenue is unchanged. That single event consumes approximately 19.05% of planned owner profit. Contract deposits, staged billing, and bounded supplier liabilities matter more than a dashboard showing impressive award face values.

Instrument the desk around evidence age and exposure, not vanity submission counts. Flag more than 10% unbilled completed work, receivables beyond contractual terms by fifteen days, or rework exceeding 10% of delivery hours; these are internal starting thresholds, not statutory standards. Require opportunity-level contribution estimates before accepting another amendment cycle. Measure buyer concentration against collected service fees and pause incremental unsecured exposure when one client exceeds 25% without a specific reserve decision. Set a zero-tolerance stop for unsupported material certifications, fabricated records, or unexplained restricted documents. False Claims Act exposure under 31 U.S.C. 3729 can include treble damages and adjusted civil penalties; small service fees do not bound potential liability for knowingly causing false claims. When an exception hits, preserve originals, isolate affected submissions, quantify the maximum plausible loss, and assign corrective ownership. Apply mandatory disclosure duties when their actual contractual and regulatory conditions are met; FAR 52.203-13 is not a universal clause in every municipal engagement. Restart only after the responsible person verifies corrected evidence and revised cash capacity. Automation should accelerate alerts and reconciliations, never manufacture eligibility, acceptance, or government authority.

sop_steps.title: Freeze the affected commitment
sop_steps.action: Pause the specific submission, enrollment source, supplier order, or invoice implicated by the exception.
sop_steps.detail: Do not disable unrelated client work automatically. Preserve original files, timestamps, approvals, and portal messages with access limited to authorized reviewers.

sop_steps.title: Build the exposure ledger
sop_steps.action: Separate earned service fees, client award value, carrier support, refunds, replacement costs, and contingent obligations.
sop_steps.detail: Record best-supported and plausible adverse outcomes. Show who owes each amount, when it could become payable, and whether any reserve or insurance actually responds.

sop_steps.title: Correct through the responsible channel
sop_steps.action: Assign the prime, ETC, client principal, or authorized contracting contact to the correction appropriate to their authority.
sop_steps.detail: Use designated counsel for material misrepresentation or disclosure questions. Do not silently edit submitted evidence or create a replacement account to bypass restrictions.

sop_steps.title: Reconcile and authorize restart
sop_steps.action: Verify corrected source evidence, revised unit economics, and sufficient unrestricted cash before resuming the affected work.
sop_steps.detail: Document the accountable owner's restart decision, reconcile resulting credits or recoveries, and add a targeted control that detects the original failure.

chapters.question_prompt: Where do high-margin deals, clients, or undervalued assets hide in government contract brokering, and what repeatable outbound/inbound sourcing system lands the first 3-to-10 wins (3–12 months)?
chapters.title: Sourcing, Demand Mining & Landing Your First Deals
chapters.subtitle: Mine SAM.gov, USAspending.gov and Municipal Records; Convert Demand into Disclosed FAR-Aware Prime/Sub Engagements
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #4, Government Contract Brokering, holds Rank #27 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: a High-Leverage Operator Play. Build a narrow bid desk around recurring facility demand, documented supplier capacity, and paid deliverables rather than speculative award commissions. This chapter maps seven sourcing plays: disclosed facility teaming, recompete intelligence, municipal budget mining, sources-sought preparation, bid-desk retainers, supplier-readiness sprints, and post-award mobilization. Only the first carries the supplied canonical play identifier; six are chapter-level operating extensions. Annual owner profit is $18,000 Conservative, $126,000 Base, and $300,000 Scaled, on recognized service fees rather than government award value. Use public evidence, measured outreach, and delivery-capacity checks to pursue the first three to ten paid engagements over 3–12 months.

sections.heading: 1. Find Purchasable Demand Before Chasing Published Bids
paragraphs: Start with one service family, two adjacent jurisdictions, and a buyer profile you can actually support. A useful opening wedge is custodial or grounds work for facilities with recurring requirements, measurable staffing, and public purchasing histories. Search SAM.gov Contract Opportunities by NAICS, place of performance, notice type, and response date; use relevant Product Service Codes to catch inconsistent labels. Pull historical award transactions from USAspending.gov, then verify the actual solicitation, amendments, and contract information against the issuing agency's records. An apparent expiration date is a research lead, not proof that a recompete will occur: options, extensions, consolidations, and cancellations change the calendar. For municipal work, inspect adopted budgets, purchasing forecasts, council agendas, bid tabs, and the city's designated vendor portal. Record the source URL, retrieval date, buying office, incumbent, estimated timing, and specific service requirement in a shared register. Separate government demand records from prospective paying clients: the agency buys performance, while a qualified prime or supplier may buy your research and coordination. That distinction prevents a large public award from masquerading as brokerage revenue and keeps outreach focused on an identifiable commercial customer with a solvable operating problem.

Use seven plays, but treat them as routes to paid work rather than seven simultaneous businesses. The supplied canonical TRACK_1 play is gsa_municipal_set_aside_facility_ghost_brokering; its permissible implementation is disclosed facility teaming, never an invisible middleman or fabricated eligibility claim. The other six chapter-level plays are recompete intelligence, municipal budget mining, sources-sought preparation, bid-desk retainers, supplier-readiness sprints, and post-award mobilization. Each must produce something a client can inspect: a verified pursuit calendar, procurement-route memo, capability response, submission package, capacity dossier, or mobilization tracker. Price defined work in advance and document acceptance; a fixed fee does not by itself resolve contingent-fee, kickback, conflict, or procurement integrity issues. Under FAR Subpart 3.4 and applicable contract clauses, review the actual arrangement, solicitation, and any claimed bona fide employee or agency exception before accepting award-linked compensation. Never sell access to an official or imply influence over source selection. For each play, the matrix supplies a small fee unit and a fallback when the underlying procurement disappears. Those units illustrate individual engagement design, not additional revenue stacked on top of the canonical annual cases. Count an engagement once even when it uses several sourcing methods.

Build a weekly signal queue rather than an indiscriminate notice feed. On Monday, review expiring awards and municipal purchasing calendars; on Tuesday, examine new sources-sought notices and draft requirements; on Wednesday, reconcile amendments and bid tabs; reserve Thursday for supplier verification and Friday for client pursuit decisions. Public-record requests should target existing records, such as executed contracts or releasable evaluation summaries, not demand that staff create custom analyses. Federal FOIA, 5 U.S.C. 552, has exemptions and timing constraints; use each municipality's applicable records process for local documents. Do not schedule a proposal around an assumed disclosure date. Strong triggers include a funded replacement requirement, a published outreach event, repeated publicly documented bid failures, or a client lacking coverage for an identified location. Weak triggers include a large ceiling value, a vendor directory entry, or an old award without current demand evidence. Preserve original files and annotate in separate notes so an amendment can be traced to its source. A simple Airtable register or Excel workbook is adequate initially; automate alerts only after manually checking a sample of matched and missed opportunities against the same written search rules.

callout.title: Read the Procurement Trail, Not Just the Notice
callout.body: Experienced bid desks earn their fees by finding verifiable operating friction before a submission deadline makes every correction expensive.
items: Compare the last two public bid tabs with current specifications; investigate scope changes before treating a price increase as available margin.
Check whether a historical award amount is an obligation, modification, or ceiling before using it to rank a pursuit.
For GSA-related demand, distinguish a GSA-issued procurement from an agency order through a GSA vehicle; verify the client's actual access route.
Keep a second dated supplier quote for critical coverage, but obtain permission before naming any supplier in a proposal.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify the Client, Procurement Route, and Delivery Structure
paragraphs: Score the paying client separately from the government opportunity. For the client, inspect current service capability, management attention, cash available for mobilization, relevant past performance, and willingness to pay for defined work regardless of award outcome. For the opportunity, score demand evidence at twenty points, procurement-route access at twenty, delivery capacity at twenty, client economics at fifteen, timing at fifteen, and evidence quality at ten. Pursue seventy-five or more, investigate sixty through seventy-four, and archive lower scores with a reason. These are internal operating thresholds, not measured industry predictors. Hard failures override the total: false eligibility, prohibited compensation, an inaccessible vehicle, missing mandatory capacity, or insufficient submission time cannot be averaged away. Verify the legal entity and UEI when relevant, review SAM.gov registration and exclusions, and confirm applicable size and program status using authoritative records and the solicitation's assigned NAICS. Municipal registration and certification rules are separate; federal status does not automatically satisfy them. Require a dated evidence link for every score. A relationship owner's optimism is not evidence, and an attractive contract ceiling cannot cure a client that cannot staff or fund the first month of performance.

For facility teaming, map every work element to the entity actually performing it, the supervisor controlling it, and the invoice that will support payment. FAR 52.219-14 and 13 CFR 125.6 can restrict subcontracting on covered set-asides; for covered service contracts, the general rule limits payments to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities to fifty percent of the amount paid by the government for contract performance, subject to applicable exceptions and measurement rules. Do not substitute a generic gross-margin calculation for that analysis. Determine which costs and entities count, and document the governing clause and program requirements. Review the ostensible subcontractor rule in 13 CFR 121.103 when a proposed subcontractor performs primary and vital requirements or creates unusual reliance. Where applicable, FAR 52.215-23 addresses excessive pass-through charges; merely forwarding invoices does not demonstrate useful coordination. A $200,000 client award and a $6,000 coordination engagement therefore remain two different economic records: only the earned $6,000 belongs in the operator's service revenue. If the structure fails, withdraw the noncompliant bid and offer disclosed subcontract performance on unrestricted work, with real responsibilities and independently supportable pricing.

Turn supplier diligence into a short evidence interview followed by document checks. Ask who supervises the site, where replacement workers come from, which locations the supplier already covers, how long its price remains valid, and which assumptions would change the quote. Verify insurance through appropriate channels, obtain client permission for reference checks, and reconcile staffing hours against the statement of work. Where federal service labor requirements apply, price the applicable wage determination and fringe obligations under the Service Contract Labor Standards statute and implementing rules before quoting labor-dependent work. Check separately for local wage, licensing, bonding, and background screening requirements. Never treat a low quote as evidence of an executable margin until these inputs agree. Record contractor availability as a dated commitment with conditions, not a permanent capability. Identify one replacement route for each critical role and test whether substitution requires buyer permission. Finally, screen the compensation chain for kickbacks under 41 U.S.C. 8702 and protect procurement information under 41 U.S.C. 2102. If someone offers confidential competitor pricing or internal evaluation material, stop the exchange, preserve the incident record securely, and escalate without using that material to shape a bid.

sections.heading: 3. Run Evidence-Led Outreach That Converts into Paid Work
paragraphs: Construct a named-account list from demonstrable fit, not purchased email volume. Begin with firms already delivering the chosen service family, companies appearing in relevant public bid tabs, and suppliers whose published capabilities match an identified geographic gap. Resolve each legal entity and record one appropriate business contact, the source of that contact, the demand trigger, and a specific deliverable you could sell. Lead with an evidence-based observation: 'The city published a facilities requirement covering three locations; your service area overlaps two. We can assess coverage, teaming, and submission requirements in a paid diagnostic.' Avoid suggesting that you represent the city. Use commercial email in accordance with 15 U.S.C. 7704, including accurate headers, a valid postal address, and a working opt-out process; honor opt-outs promptly and within the statutory period. Keep phone and platform outreach within applicable rules and the recipient's preferences. Government communications belong through the solicitation's designated channel, especially during restricted communication periods. The person buying your service is normally the supplier's owner, business-development lead, or operations manager, not an official being asked to steer an award toward your client or introduce privileged information into the pursuit.

Use a five-touch, fifteen-business-day sequence with a reason for every contact. Day one sends the public trigger and a two-sentence fit hypothesis. Day three uses a permitted business call to confirm who owns pursuit decisions. Day six sends one useful finding, such as a mandatory site visit or documented coverage gap. Day ten offers a twenty-minute qualification discussion with a sample deliverable. Day fifteen closes the sequence and offers an explicit way to decline further contact. Stop immediately after an opt-out or clear refusal; suppress duplicate campaigns across the team. Support inbound demand with a narrow landing page showing a redacted pursuit brief, a clear service scope, and one booking action. Publish source-linked procurement notes without client confidentiality breaches, copied proprietary specifications, or implied government endorsement. An APEX Accelerator can help a client understand readiness requirements; do not claim that publicly supported counseling is your proprietary service. Track inbound and outbound separately because referral leads behave differently from cold contacts. Attribute a mandate to its original source and record assisted touches without counting the same paying client twice. The purpose is qualified commercial conversations, not a flattering dashboard of impressions and opens.

For planning, model a mature ninety-day cohort of two hundred researched accounts, one hundred forty verified reachable contacts, twenty-eight substantive conversations, fourteen qualified opportunities, seven scoped proposals, and three signed paid mandates. The successive conversion assumptions are seventy percent, twenty percent, fifty percent, fifty percent, and approximately forty-three percent; the end-to-end mandate rate is one and a half percent. These are testable operating hypotheses, not observed market benchmarks. Early cohorts may produce no mandates, and the first three to ten wins remain a six-to-eighteen-month objective as references and procurement timing develop. Define a win as a signed service engagement with a funded initial milestone, then track government awards separately. A $4,000 diagnostic should specify the records reviewed, suitability assessment, supplier checks, delivery date, and acceptance process; later work requires a separate scope. When a prospect says it can search SAM.gov itself, agree and show the missing verification labor. When it demands payment only after award, explain the actual deliverable and review any alternative compensation structure before accepting it. When it asks for a guaranteed outcome, offer a bounded research product instead. Declining an unsuitable engagement preserves capacity for customers willing to purchase work you can control.

sections.heading: 4. Turn Early Mandates into a Reconciled, Repeatable Bid Desk
paragraphs: Reconcile every sourcing decision to the canonical fee business. Conservative revenue is $120,000, with $102,000 total costs and $18,000 owner net profit at fifteen percent, using two full-time employees and three contractors. Base revenue is $560,000, with $434,000 total costs and $126,000 owner net profit at twenty-two and a half percent, using the same team count. Scaled revenue is $1,000,000, with $700,000 total costs and $300,000 owner net profit at thirty percent, using three full-time employees and four contractors. Illustrative annual fee recipes are six clients at $20,000, fourteen at $40,000, and twenty at $50,000 respectively, with all amounts earned through delivered service periods and accepted work. They are alternative cases, not additive targets or a claim that every first-year client reaches a full annual fee. Individual play contributions exclude shared overhead and therefore cannot be substituted for these net margins. The Conservative cost envelope is particularly tight for its stated staffing: obtain actual compensation, contractor, insurance, and software quotes before deciding whether it is executable. If local costs exceed the envelope, report the shortfall rather than silently treating unpaid founder effort as free labor or changing the canonical profit figure.

Run delivery from a single pursuit record with controlled access and a named owner for each deadline. Store original notices, amendments, client representations, supplier quotes, scope versions, and acceptance records in an organized SharePoint or Google Drive workspace appropriate to the data involved. These ordinary tools are not automatic substitutes for contract-specific security requirements; assess any restricted information before receiving it. Use calendar reminders for the questions cutoff, required visits, pricing expiry, review date, and submission receipt. Automate notification and checklist creation, but require a person to resolve changed requirements and confirm the final package. Maintain an amendment acknowledgment log and a submission rehearsal that checks file limits, portal credentials, and authorized signers without transmitting a premature bid. If a supplier fails, compare the replacement against the original qualification evidence and applicable substitution rules. If a buyer cancels, pause unearned tasks and apply the engagement's cancellation terms. If a client delays payment, follow written collection and stop-work provisions rather than assuming the agency's payment timetable governs your separate service agreement. Award uncertainty, payment delays, and supplier failure deserve distinct incident codes because each requires a different change to sourcing, scope, or delivery.

Use the first six months to validate a niche and a repeatable paid diagnostic, not to hire ahead of assumed awards. Months one and two establish the signal register, supplier evidence, service scope, and first researched account cohorts. Months three through six test conversations and proposals while building references from completed work. Months seven through twelve concentrate on the strongest client segment and renew only engagements with actual recurring deliverables. Months thirteen through eighteen can extend the first three wins toward ten, subject to observed demand and delivery capacity. Review cohort conversion, acquisition effort, recognized fees, cash receipts, revision hours, and referral sources every month. Calculate acquisition cost from attributable outreach labor and spending divided by new paying clients; compare it with collected contribution, not a government contract's face value. The stated startup capital range is $20,000–$90,000 and monthly operating expense range is $5,000–$25,000; neither substitutes for a dated cash forecast. Retain enough runway for delayed buying cycles and model milestone collections explicitly. Expand only when repeatable service delivery, measured demand, and cash support the next capacity step. A smaller verified pipeline is more valuable than a large list of awards the business cannot lawfully support.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #4, Government Contract Brokering, holds Rank #27 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter turns seven mapped plays into an executable service operation: federal opportunity triage, municipal bid-desk support, prime/sub teaming, response production, supplier verification, invoice reconciliation, and Section 179D allocation documentation. The production reference uses six ordered SQLite modules, immutable balanced postings, serialized transitions, and replay-safe collection records. A worked quarter separates new prospect cohorts from seven established customers, recognizes $140,000 in earned fees, and produces $31,500 in operating profit. Annual owner-profit cases remain $18,000 Conservative, $126,000 Base, and $300,000 Scaled. Government award value and tax deductions never become operator revenue; accepted services, collectible invoices, and controlled delivery costs do.

sections.heading: 1. Convert authorized demand into seven bounded service plays
paragraphs: Start with the customer relationship, not the procurement notice. The bid desk sells defined research, coordination, documentation, and delivery services to an identified client under a signed scope. It does not sell access to contracting officers or promise an award. Record the client's legal entity, authorized sponsor, billing contact, permitted systems, purchasing objective, and responsibility for final representations. Pull federal notices from SAM.gov through authorized interfaces; preserve the solicitation identifier, amendment number, attachment digest, retrieval time, and submission deadline with its stated time zone. Municipal opportunities require their own portal instructions and local purchasing rules rather than an assumption that the FAR applies everywhere. Score fit only after checking eligibility, delivery capacity, mandatory registrations, and actual response time. A high-value notice with an impossible site visit is a rejected opportunity, not a pipeline asset. For federally funded local purchases, determine whether 2 CFR 200.318 and related procurement standards apply. Separate public-source research from restricted information: 41 U.S.C. 2102 prohibits specified disclosures and receipt of protected procurement information before award. Quarantine unsolicited source-selection material and escalate through the client's designated reviewer without circulating it through the production team.

Use seven explicitly bounded plays rather than a vague brokerage mandate. Federal triage creates an evidence-backed shortlist; the municipal desk maintains jurisdiction-specific bid instructions; teaming support documents genuine prime and subcontractor responsibilities; response production assembles compliant artifacts; supplier verification tests capacity; invoice reconciliation traces accepted work to payment; allocation documentation supports eligible Section 179D projects. These are chapter-level operating mappings, not seven separate promises of incremental revenue. Price an accepted service unit at $2,000 in the worked model, with a $1,550 average fully allocated delivery budget and $450 operating contribution after that allocation. Seventy units produce $140,000 of quarterly fees, $108,500 of costs, and $31,500 of profit. One unit might be a bounded solicitation review or a separately accepted supplier dossier; the statement of work defines the actual deliverable and revision allowance. Never charge twice because the same artifact supports two plays. Review FAR Subpart 3.4 and applicable contingent-fee clauses before accepting compensation arrangements. Fixed pricing does not cure an otherwise prohibited activity, and a percentage of an award is not automatically permissible merely because the invoice calls it consulting. Suspend unsupported structures and retain only independently lawful, documented services.

The mapped play section_179d_municipal_deduction_allocation_arbitrage requires especially disciplined language and evidence. Under TRACK_1, coordinate eligible government or specified tax-exempt building owners, qualifying designers, and independent energy certifiers; the deliverable is an allocation documentation file, not ownership of a freely transferable deduction. Before pricing, establish building ownership, construction timing, qualifying designer activity, technical certification requirements, and the applicable version of 26 U.S.C. 179D. The statutory termination for property whose construction begins after June 30, 2026 makes construction-start evidence an essential intake field. Also resolve applicable prevailing-wage and apprenticeship conditions before anyone models enhanced deduction amounts. A $2,000 documentation engagement recognizes only $2,000 of service revenue; even an independently supported $100,000 deduction estimate contributes zero additional operator revenue. The designer's tax position remains separate from the desk's ledger. Obtain owner authorization, certifier independence evidence, allocation signatures, and a version-controlled supporting file before marking the documentation milestone accepted. If eligibility, allocation authority, or tax treatment is unresolved, pause allocation, obtain independent tax review, and offer fixed-fee documentation support only for eligible projects. Do not manufacture eligibility by relabeling a referral as design work.

sections.heading: 2. Install a six-module ledger with serialized, replay-safe workflow
paragraphs: The reference table contains six executable modules that share one Python namespace; concatenate their code cells in numbered order and run them with Python 3.9 or later. They use only the standard library and a local SQLite database. The final module executes assertions against isolated test databases; it does not contact SAM.gov, move money, or access customer systems. Provision the production database once, then give each worker its own connection. All business mutations acquire BEGIN IMMEDIATE before checking existing records, which serializes competing writers and closes the usual check-then-insert race. Unique constraints independently protect source identities, milestones, and posting keys. A repeated request with identical content returns its prior result; reuse with different content raises an error. Busy-lock failures are safe failures rather than permission to bypass the transaction. Retry the same request identifier after bounded backoff. Keep the database on a supported local filesystem, not a shared network drive. This design addresses concurrent mutations inside one database; external portals and bank systems remain outside its transaction boundary. No local schema can make an unrelated remote submission exactly once without the remote system's own deduplication contract.

Treat verification as an evidence-bearing state transition, not a visual status label. Intake records begin staged; eligible records become verified, unresolved records become held, and client-accepted service milestones may enter accepted. Every transition supplies the expected prior state, a stable event key, an actor, and evidence. A stale worker cannot overwrite a newer decision because the state comparison occurs while holding the write transaction. The evidence requirements establish workflow completeness, not the truth of client claims; human reviewers still inspect the referenced source files. Enforce authentication and reviewer permissions in the application before exposing these functions. The table deliberately treats escrow as a noncustodial boundary: held means work is paused, not that the desk possesses customer funds. There is no escrow release or payment initiation function. If a separate authorized arrangement uses a regulated custodian, record its confirmed status as external evidence and keep its funds outside this service ledger. For prime/sub work, review FAR 52.215-23 when included, 13 CFR 125.6 where applicable, and relevant affiliation and set-aside requirements before accepting the structure. A clean database cannot rescue an impermissible arrangement.

The ledger records balanced account pairs rather than unbalanced free-form lines. Accepted invoices debit accounts receivable and credit service revenue; matched collections debit cash and credit receivables; paid operating costs debit expense and credit cash. Amounts are positive integer cents, and every receipt has a bank-scoped transaction identifier. Database triggers prevent invoice mutation, journal edits, duplicate revenue recognition, and collections exceeding the invoice balance. The reference intentionally supports one invoice allocation per bank transaction; split remittances, credits, refunds, prepayments, and disputed corrections require a separately designed extension rather than manual database edits. Preserve rejected imports outside the posted ledger until reviewed. The reconciliation view reports earned fees, cash receipts, paid expenses, operating profit, and operating cash flow separately. Opening capital affects cash but never service revenue. Protect the database with service-account file permissions, encrypted backups, and tested restoration; append-only triggers are application controls, not protection against a privileged database administrator. Add an external audit-log destination before multi-user deployment. For production cash reporting, reconcile the imported receipt set to bank statements and preserve statement identifiers alongside the event keys used by the posting functions.

Module 2: Intake immutable source snapshots and deterministic opportunity scores

def intake(db, source, source_key, payload):
    required_text(source)
    required_text(source_key)
    for field in ("eligible", "capacity_confirmed"):
        if type(payload.get(field)) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("eligibility and capacity must be explicit")
    remaining = payload.get("days_remaining")
    if type(remaining) is not int or remaining < 0:
        raise ValueError("nonnegative deadline interval required")
    required_text(payload.get("document_sha"))
    score = (
        40 * int(payload["eligible"])
        + 30 * int(payload["capacity_confirmed"])
        + 30 * int(remaining >= 10)
    )
    fingerprint = digest(payload)
    with atomic(db):
        prior = db.execute(
            "SELECT id, payload_sha, score FROM opportunity "
            "WHERE source = ? AND source_key = ?",
            (source, source_key),
        ).fetchone()
        if prior:
            if prior[1:] != (fingerprint, score):
                raise ValueError("source identity reused with altered content")
            return prior[0]
        cursor = db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO opportunity "
            "(source, source_key, payload_sha, score) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (source, source_key, fingerprint, score),
        )
        return cursor.lastrowid
Identical source replays return one record while altered snapshots require distinct amendment identities
Use authorized public-source retrieval upstream; preserve original attachments in controlled evidence storage

Module 4: Recognize accepted milestones and import matched bank receipts

def _entry(db, event_key, invoice_id, booked_on, debit, credit, amount):
    if not db.in_transaction:
        raise RuntimeError("posting requires the business transaction")
    required_text(event_key)
    day(booked_on)
    cents(amount)
    values = (invoice_id, booked_on, debit, credit, amount)
    prior = db.execute(
        "SELECT invoice_id, booked_on, debit, credit, amount_cents "
        "FROM journal WHERE event_key = ?",
        (event_key,),
    ).fetchone()
    if prior:
        if prior != values:
            raise ValueError("posting key reused with altered content")
        return
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO journal "
        "(event_key, invoice_id, booked_on, debit, credit, amount_cents) "
        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
        (event_key,) + values,
    )

def issue_invoice(db, invoice_key, opportunity_id, milestone_key, booked_on, amount):
    required_text(invoice_key)
    required_text(milestone_key)
    day(booked_on)
    cents(amount)
    values = (opportunity_id, milestone_key, booked_on, amount)
    with atomic(db):
        prior = db.execute(
            "SELECT id, opportunity_id, milestone_key, booked_on, amount_cents "
            "FROM invoice WHERE invoice_key = ?",
            (invoice_key,),
        ).fetchone()
        if prior:
            if prior[1:] != values:
                raise ValueError("invoice key reused with altered content")
            return prior[0]
        state = db.execute(
            "SELECT state FROM opportunity WHERE id = ?",
            (opportunity_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if state != ("accepted",):
            raise ValueError("accepted service evidence required")
        cursor = db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO invoice "
            "(invoice_key, opportunity_id, milestone_key, booked_on, amount_cents) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (invoice_key,) + values,
        )
        invoice_id = cursor.lastrowid
        _entry(
            db, "invoice:" + invoice_key, invoice_id, booked_on,
            "ar", "service_revenue", amount,
        )
        return invoice_id

def collect(db, bank_transaction_key, invoice_id, booked_on, amount):
    required_text(bank_transaction_key)
    with atomic(db):
        _entry(
            db, "bank:" + bank_transaction_key, invoice_id, booked_on,
            "cash", "ar", amount,
        )

def pay_expense(db, expense_key, booked_on, amount):
    required_text(expense_key)
    with atomic(db):
        _entry(
            db, "expense:" + expense_key, None, booked_on,
            "expense", "cash", amount,
        )

def contribute_capital(db, contribution_key, booked_on, amount):
    required_text(contribution_key)
    with atomic(db):
        _entry(
            db, "capital:" + contribution_key, None, booked_on,
            "cash", "owner_capital", amount,
        )
Invoice creation and revenue posting commit together; repeated bank identities cannot create duplicate collections
Import confirmed receipts only; split remittances and corrective accounting require reviewed extensions before use
Module 5: Expose monthly earnings and independent cash reconciliation views

VIEWS = """
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS monthly_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    substr(booked_on, 1, 7) AS month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN credit = 'service_revenue'
        THEN amount_cents ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN debit = 'cash' AND credit = 'ar'
        THEN amount_cents ELSE 0 END) AS receipts_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN debit = 'expense'
        THEN amount_cents ELSE 0 END) AS expense_cents,
    SUM(CASE
        WHEN credit = 'service_revenue' THEN amount_cents
        WHEN debit = 'expense' THEN -amount_cents
        ELSE 0 END) AS profit_cents,
    SUM(CASE
        WHEN debit = 'cash' AND credit = 'ar' THEN amount_cents
        WHEN debit = 'expense' THEN -amount_cents
        ELSE 0 END) AS operating_cash_cents
FROM journal
GROUP BY substr(booked_on, 1, 7);

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS receivables AS
SELECT
    i.id AS invoice_id,
    i.invoice_key,
    i.amount_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN j.credit = 'ar'
        THEN j.amount_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS collected_cents,
    i.amount_cents - COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN j.credit = 'ar'
        THEN j.amount_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS open_cents
FROM invoice AS i
LEFT JOIN journal AS j ON j.invoice_id = i.id
GROUP BY i.id, i.invoice_key, i.amount_cents;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS cash_position AS
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE
    WHEN debit = 'cash' THEN amount_cents
    WHEN credit = 'cash' THEN -amount_cents
    ELSE 0 END), 0) AS cash_cents
FROM journal;
"""

def install_views(db):
    if db.in_transaction:
        raise RuntimeError("install views outside business transactions")
    db.executescript(VIEWS)
Revenue, receipts, expenses, profit, and capital remain distinct through separately calculated account movements
Join statement evidence upstream and compare every posted bank identity against cleared statement transactions
Module 6: Exercise cohort arithmetic, rejected mutations, and simultaneous replays

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from pathlib import Path

def must_reject(action):
    try:
        action()
    except (ValueError, sqlite3.IntegrityError):
        return
    raise AssertionError("invalid operation unexpectedly succeeded")

def run_reference_checks():
    db = open_db(":memory:")
    install_views(db)
    payload = {
        "eligible": True,
        "capacity_confirmed": True,
        "days_remaining": 21,
        "document_sha": "illustrative-source-digest",
    }
    opportunity_id = intake(db, "client-scope", "established-cohort-v1", payload)
    assert intake(db, "client-scope", "established-cohort-v1", payload) == opportunity_id
    verified = {
        "evidence_ref": "review-file-001",
        "eligibility_checked": True,
        "fee_structure_checked": True,
        "conflicts_checked": True,
    }
    advance(db, "verify-001", opportunity_id, "staged", "verified",
            "authorized-reviewer", verified)
    advance(db, "accept-001", opportunity_id, "verified", "accepted",
            "authorized-reviewer", {
                "evidence_ref": "accepted-service-batch",
                "client_acceptance_ref": "signed-monthly-milestone-schedule",
            })
    must_reject(lambda: advance(
        db, "stale-001", opportunity_id, "verified", "held",
        "authorized-reviewer", {"evidence_ref": "late-review"},
    ))
    contribute_capital(db, "opening", "2027-01-01", 6000000)
    first = issue_invoice(db, "m1", opportunity_id, "month-1", "2027-01-05", 4000000)
    second = issue_invoice(db, "m2", opportunity_id, "month-2", "2027-02-05", 5000000)
    third = issue_invoice(db, "m3", opportunity_id, "month-3", "2027-03-05", 5000000)
    collect(db, "account-a:001", first, "2027-01-25", 3000000)
    collect(db, "account-a:001", first, "2027-01-25", 3000000)
    must_reject(lambda: collect(
        db, "account-a:001", first, "2027-01-25", 3000001,
    ))
    collect(db, "account-a:002", first, "2027-02-10", 1000000)
    collect(db, "account-a:003", second, "2027-02-25", 3000000)
    collect(db, "account-a:004", second, "2027-03-10", 2000000)
    collect(db, "account-a:005", third, "2027-03-25", 3000000)
    must_reject(lambda: collect(
        db, "account-a:overpayment", third, "2027-03-26", 2000001,
    ))
    for key, booked_on, amount in (
        ("m1", "2027-01-28", 3600000),
        ("m2", "2027-02-28", 3600000),
        ("m3", "2027-03-28", 3650000),
    ):
        pay_expense(db, key, booked_on, amount)
    rows = db.execute(
        "SELECT revenue_cents, receipts_cents, expense_cents, "
        "profit_cents, operating_cash_cents "
        "FROM monthly_reconciliation ORDER BY month"
    ).fetchall()
    assert rows == [
        (4000000, 3000000, 3600000, 400000, -600000),
        (5000000, 4000000, 3600000, 1400000, 400000),
        (5000000, 5000000, 3650000, 1350000, 1350000),
    ]
    assert db.execute("SELECT SUM(open_cents) FROM receivables").fetchone()[0] == 2000000
    assert db.execute("SELECT cash_cents FROM cash_position").fetchone()[0] == 7150000
    assert sum(row[0] for row in rows) * 4 == 56000000
    assert sum(row[3] for row in rows) * 4 == 12600000
    assert db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall() == []
    assert db.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0] == "ok"
    must_reject(lambda: db.execute(
        "UPDATE journal SET amount_cents = amount_cents + 1 WHERE id = 1"
    ))
    db.close()

    with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        path = str(Path(directory) / "race-test.sqlite3")
        setup = open_db(path)
        setup.close()

        def competing_post(_):
            worker = open_db(path, initialize=False)
            try:
                pay_expense(worker, "same-expense", "2027-01-02", 10000)
            finally:
                worker.close()

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
            list(pool.map(competing_post, range(12)))
        check = open_db(path, initialize=False)
        assert check.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(amount_cents) FROM journal"
        ).fetchone() == (1, 10000)
        check.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_reference_checks()
    print("Reference ledger checks passed.")

sections.heading: 3. Walk three prospect cohorts without inventing a 90-day award cycle
paragraphs: The Worked 90-Day Cohort Walk begins with seven established customers sourced through an earlier six-to-eighteen-month development cycle. It is an operating quarter, not a claim that a new desk can win seven government contracts in ninety days. Each customer buys an average of ten accepted $2,000 service units across the quarter, producing $20,000 per customer and $140,000 in aggregate earned fees. The work schedule contains twenty accepted units in Month 1, twenty-five in Month 2, and twenty-five in Month 3. Their recognition totals are therefore $40,000, $50,000, and $50,000. Neither solicitation face value nor prospective award size appears in those figures. New prospects are tracked separately: Month 1 starts eighteen leads, Month 2 starts twenty, and Month 3 starts twenty-two. Eligibility scrubs, commercial losses, parked opportunities, and qualified follow-ups exhaust each monthly lead cohort without double counting. Eleven qualified follow-ups remain potential future business; none is treated as a signed customer or recognized revenue during the quarter. This separation makes the model useful for an established practice while preserving the startup's actual sales-cycle constraint.

Assume zero opening receivables and $60,000 of opening owner-funded cash. In Month 1, customers pay $30,000 against $40,000 of accepted invoices, leaving $10,000 receivable. Month 2 collects that $10,000 plus $30,000 against its own $50,000 invoices, leaving $20,000 receivable. Month 3 collects the prior $20,000 plus $30,000 against its own $50,000, again leaving $20,000 outstanding. Paid operating costs are $36,000, $36,000, and $36,500. Monthly operating cash movement is consequently negative $6,000, positive $4,000, and positive $13,500; ending cash is $54,000, $58,000, and $71,500. Quarterly profit is $31,500, while operating cash generated is only $11,500 because $20,000 remains in receivables. The opening contribution is funding, not profit. The illustration assumes all modeled operating costs are both incurred and paid in the quarter, with no opening liabilities, advance billings, distributions, or capital expenditures. Adding any of those items requires an explicit bridge rather than a silent adjustment to the owner-profit number. Track disputed invoices separately from ordinary processing delays before deciding that aging is harmless.

Annualize the quarter's earnings, not its collection shortfall: four times $140,000 equals the Base revenue of $560,000, and four times $31,500 equals $126,000 of annual owner net profit. The implied annual expense budget is $434,000 and the margin is exactly 22.5%. Repeating the same quarterly receivable increase four times would accumulate $80,000 of additional working-capital demand; it is not a collection plan. Require Month 4 follow-up on the remaining $20,000 and build a rolling thirteen-week cash forecast from actual customer payment behavior. The two full-time staff and three contractors must fit within the cost envelope. Here, quarterly loaded employee cost is $42,000, tools are $6,000, and insurance plus accounting is $6,000, yielding $18,000 monthly fixed overhead. The three-contractor pool supplies $54,500 of variable delivery and specialist review across the quarter. Thus total monthly expense can exceed the metadata's $5,000–$25,000 monthly operating-overhead range without hiding the additional direct delivery cost. Contractor allocations reflect purchased capacity, not three additional full-time salaries. Any staffing plan that cannot deliver seventy accepted units within this budget must change scope, price, or throughput.

sections.heading: 4. Close the evidence loop and scale only collectible production
paragraphs: Close each week with an exception review organized by economic consequence. Award uncertainty belongs in pipeline probability, not in a receivable. Customer acceptance disputes belong in the delivery queue with the contractual revision allowance visible. Bank transactions lacking a valid invoice match remain unposted until resolved. Supplier failure requires a replacement plan, revised delivery dates, and an assessment of the client's actual contractual obligations. Payment delays require named follow-up responsibility and a cash forecast update, not optimistic comments in the customer record. FAR Subpart 32.9 and the Prompt Payment Act inform federal payment administration where applicable, but the desk's private service invoice follows its own customer contract; federal payment protections do not automatically pass through to every consultant. Preserve government acceptance and payment evidence when the customer is a prime contractor, while recognizing that the desk's debtor remains its contracting customer. Escalate repeated delays before purchasing more contractor capacity. A customer with an impressive award notice but weak collection behavior can consume more working capital than a smaller, punctual account with narrowly scoped service requirements.

Run the production board on accepted units, rework hours, and aged receivables rather than bid count. At the Base case, 280 annual $2,000 units average roughly 5.4 accepted units per week across fifty-two weeks; actual staffing must allow for holidays and deadline bunching. The fully allocated target cost remains $1,550 per unit, but individual scopes need their own labor estimate and specialist review allowance. Solicitation alerts automate discovery, bid calendars automate reminders, and checklist generation automates requirement tracking. None should autonomously certify eligibility, sign representations, or invent supplier capacity. Require human review for final source interpretations and client-facing commitments. Track the percentage of delivered artifacts returned for material correction; rising rework consumes the $450 unit margin before annual financial reports reveal the problem. For each repeated defect, update the requirement mapping or intake question that should have prevented it. Keep solicitation-specific evidence separate from reusable templates so a past certification cannot silently migrate into a new bid. Limit work in progress when review capacity, rather than drafting capacity, becomes the binding constraint.

Maintain the three canonical scenarios as separate operating configurations. Conservative revenue of $120,000 at 15% margin leaves $18,000 owner net profit and $102,000 of costs with two full-time staff and three contractors; this thin cost envelope requires explicitly validated compensation and capacity assumptions. Base revenue of $560,000 at 22.5% margin leaves $126,000 after $434,000 of costs with the same headcount. Scaled revenue of $1,000,000 at 30% margin leaves $300,000 after $700,000 of costs with three full-time staff and four contractors. Do not obtain the Scaled margin by silently removing owner labor, specialist review, insurance, or collection work from costs. Before expanding, validate contractor availability, review throughput, customer concentration, and the minimum cash balance under delayed-payment stress. The $20,000–$90,000 startup capital range must support the actual six-to-eighteen-month first-deal horizon; the illustrated $60,000 opening balance belongs to an already operating cohort. If runway is inadequate, reduce committed capacity or secure funding before accepting more scope. Growth is an increase in accepted, collectible service production, not a larger spreadsheet of government opportunities.

Its edge comes from verified procurement evidence, not a larger contact list. This chapter maps seven operator plays: solicitation discovery, award intelligence, prime qualification, supplier discovery, lawful teaming, bid control, and post-award monitoring. sections.heading: 1. Build an authoritative source directory around seven billable plays
paragraphs: Give Candidate #4 seven explicit operating lanes before buying subscriptions: P1 solicitation discovery, P2 award intelligence, P3 prime qualification, P4 supplier discovery, P5 lawful teaming, P6 bid control, and P7 post-award monitoring. These are this chapter's operational mapping, not seven separate revenue forecasts. P1 finds actionable notices; P2 identifies buying patterns; P3 checks whether a proposed prime can actually perform; P4 develops supplier alternatives; P5 documents a permitted relationship; P6 controls submissions; P7 tracks delivery and payment dependencies. Assign the first full-time employee to capture and client decisions and the second to data operations and bid calendars. Use three scoped contractors for procurement review, supplier diligence, and proposal or delivery support. Contractor count does not imply five full-time salaries. Record hours, turnaround commitments, and coverage explicitly. Every source must serve a lane, produce a named artifact, and have an escalation owner. A notice without a responsible reviewer is merely inventory. An award record without transaction interpretation is potentially misleading. A vendor profile without entity verification is a lead, not a qualified partner. Start with two agency families and one municipality so the five-person pod can inspect evidence rather than spend its week maintaining connectors.

Use the directory below as a source register, not as a promise of universal API access. Cost entries distinguish free public records from separately priced delivery, analytics, and account features. Refresh entries describe desk retrieval targets or publication dependence, not provider service commitments. Check current documentation and account entitlements when configuring each connector; numeric quotas and commercial prices can change. SAM.gov opportunity records support discovery, while the issuing office's solicitation documents and amendments establish the working requirements. USAspending supports spending analysis, but obligations, outlays, ceilings, and modifications answer different questions. Municipal notices often point into another portal for attachments, registration, or submission. Preserve that chain instead of treating the first search result as the complete procurement. A published notice may arrive after a portal update, and a vendor email may arrive after both. Store publication time, retrieval time, and the source's own update field separately. Never manufacture a source timestamp when only retrieval time exists. For an active pursuit, subscribe to official notifications and inspect the issuing portal on the bid calendar's schedule. The directory's fallback is an alternate retrieval route, not authority to override newer instructions or extend a deadline.

Federal and municipal evidence require different identifiers. Carry the federal notice identifier, solicitation number, agency hierarchy, office, NAICS, product or service code, and place of performance as distinct fields. Link awards using the award identifier plus awarding agency and relevant parent award identifiers; a short award number alone can collide. For entities, preserve UEI, CAGE when applicable, legal name, address, and registration status without assuming every municipal supplier has federal identifiers. Keep municipal vendor and solicitation identifiers in their own namespaces. Use Census NAICS definitions for classification interpretation, but do not replace the solicitation's assigned code with a classifier's preferred label. P2 research can combine USAspending transactions with source award notices to identify repeat buyers and incumbent concentration. It cannot establish an incumbent's actual profit or the government's next buying decision. P3 and P4 can combine SAM registration, exclusions, SBA profiles, and supplier documents, but each proves a different proposition. A registry entry does not establish available capacity. A certification claim needs program-specific verification. Record the question each source answers so analysts stop turning one credible fact into several unsupported conclusions during qualification meetings and client-facing opportunity reviews.
