callout.title: Four habits that outperform a larger subscription stack
callout.body: The desk wins through evidence timing, identifier discipline, and selective attention rather than indiscriminate collection.
items: For P1 and P6, preserve attachment hashes alongside notice identifiers; a replaced attachment deserves review even when the title remains identical.
For P2, inspect award modifications before describing an incumbent's contract size; cumulative ceilings and individual obligations are different measures.
For P3 and P4, match UEI or jurisdiction-specific company identifiers before names; similarly named suppliers can have unrelated eligibility and delivery records.
For P5, keep a written workshare model before introducing a prime and subcontractor; enthusiastic introductions cannot repair a prohibited performance structure.

sections.heading: 2. Run an evidence-first enrichment waterfall with reversible joins
paragraphs: Implement the enrichment waterfall as a sequence of questions, not a sequence of vendors. First retrieve the authoritative notice and its attachments. Second resolve the issuing office, deadline, submission channel, set-aside designation, and required qualifications. Third identify likely suppliers from existing client records, official registrations, and program directories. Fourth enrich unresolved corporate relationships through a licensed commercial source. Fifth ask the supplier for evidence that public records cannot establish: current production capacity, insurance, delivery commitments, pricing validity, and available personnel. Stop enrichment when the next field cannot change a pursuit decision. The data operator owns collection, the capture lead owns interpretation, and the relevant contractor reviews exceptions within a defined service window. Keep the original value, normalized value, source locator, retrieval timestamp, and matching rationale for every material field. Label deterministic identifier matches separately from name-and-address candidates. Never merge two entities solely because a commercial database assigns a shared domain. Parent companies, operating subsidiaries, and joint ventures can carry different registrations and obligations. Make merges reversible with an explicit linkage record rather than overwriting source rows. This lets P3 qualification and P4 discovery share data without turning uncertain research into an asserted legal identity.

A small stdlib-based pipeline can begin with urllib.request for permitted HTTP requests, json for payloads, sqlite3 for structured records, hashlib for attachment fingerprints, and logging for execution events. Keep downloaded evidence outside the database and store its content hash, byte length, media type, and authorized storage reference. Save retrieval parameters without API secrets. Use an append-only raw layer, a normalized layer, and a decision layer containing human assessments. Fetch overlapping update windows because late publication and corrected records can defeat a simple last-seen timestamp. Deduplicate using source-specific keys and content versions, not titles. Advance a retrieval checkpoint only after every page in that window has been stored and validated. Retry network failures and appropriate server errors with bounded exponential backoff and jitter; honor Retry-After when supplied. Authentication errors require credential or permission review, not repeated retries. Reject unexpected HTML login pages masquerading as successful downloads. Store provider quotas as connector configuration instead of assuming one universal request budget. Keep the scheduler modest enough that the second full-time employee can understand every failed job and restore essential bid-calendar coverage manually during an outage without depending on an unavailable specialist.

Treat dates, money, and amendments as separate normalization problems. Preserve the deadline exactly as published, its stated timezone, and an explicitly verified UTC conversion. Python 3.9 zoneinfo can handle named zones when timezone data is available; never silently substitute the workstation's local zone. Escalate ambiguous abbreviations to the issuing office through the permitted question channel. Store monetary values using decimal.Decimal during transformation and exact decimal text or integer minor units in SQLite. Keep award ceilings, obligations, deobligations, and desk service fees in different fields. Version solicitation attachments independently from notice metadata because either can change alone. For P6, an amendment event must create a review task, identify affected requirements, and record whether acknowledgment is required. For P7, supplier milestones and invoice events should come from the authorized client's records, with public award data serving as context rather than a receivables ledger. Restrict client files by project and avoid copying sensitive proposal content into broad research indexes. Public access does not eliminate purpose limitations or contractual restrictions. Retain the smallest useful contact dataset, prefer role-based procurement contacts, and document deletion rules for expired research copies while preserving required bid evidence under the client engagement's retention schedule.

sections.heading: 3. Diagnose silent failures before they become missed bids or bad structures
paragraphs: Measure source health separately from business activity. A job that returns HTTP 200 can still retrieve a login page, an empty result caused by a changed filter, or only the first page of a large response. Maintain connector tests for expected media type, required keys, date parsing, page coverage, and attachment accessibility. Compare counts with recent comparable windows, but investigate deviations rather than declaring every quiet holiday an outage. Use a small fixture set containing known amendments, multiple pages, duplicate notices, negative award adjustments, and missing optional fields. Python unittest can exercise these cases without making live requests. urllib.error distinguishes HTTP and network failures; json identifies malformed payloads; sqlite3 queries expose duplicate identifiers and orphaned attachments. Optional workstation tools such as curl and jq accelerate diagnosis but are not dependencies of the stdlib pipeline. Never paste API keys, client proposal material, or restricted attachments into public debugging services. Save redacted request metadata so another authorized operator can reproduce a failure. The useful incident report states which sources and pursuit windows were affected, which manual checks replaced automation, and whether any client deadline or requirement decision remained unverified after recovery.

Apply procurement rules to the proposed service and relationship, not merely to the data source. FAR Subpart 3.4 and FAR 52.203-5 address contingent-fee arrangements, with defined exceptions that require factual review; calling a payment a consulting fee does not settle its treatment. 41 U.S.C. 2102 restricts disclosure and obtaining of covered bid, proposal, and source-selection information before award. A person offering an internal evaluation spreadsheet is not providing ordinary public-record enrichment. Under 41 U.S.C. 8702, kickbacks connected to covered prime contracts and subcontracts are prohibited. Structure P5 introductions and supplier payments accordingly, with a documented service scope and no hidden compensation for favorable treatment. FAR 52.215-23, where included, addresses excessive pass-through charges; 13 CFR 125.6 establishes limitations on subcontracting for covered set-aside arrangements. Evaluate applicable exceptions, contract type, similarly situated entities, performance period, and solicitation clauses rather than applying a universal percentage to every procurement. Municipal transactions require their own local rules and solicitation terms. The procurement-review contractor documents these determinations, while the capture lead ensures that the supplier list, workshare model, and fee agreement reflect the same facts before a recommendation reaches the client.

Use adversarial operational tests against your own workflow without probing agency systems beyond authorized access. Change a stored deadline in a test fixture and confirm that the calendar receives a review task rather than an unreviewed overwrite. Replace an attachment with different bytes under the same filename and confirm the hash comparison raises an amendment investigation. Introduce two suppliers with similar names and different UEIs, then confirm that enrichment keeps them separate. Simulate throttling, expired credentials, an incomplete final page, and a timezone conversion failure. In each case, the pipeline should retain the last verified record, mark freshness accurately, and identify the person responsible for manual coverage. Do not label stale records current because the scheduler ran successfully. Give P6 deadlines higher operational priority than P2 historical research when capacity is constrained. For P7, simulate a supplier milestone slipping while the public award record stays unchanged; the client-facing exception must still appear. Review incidents weekly with both full-time employees and only the contractor needed for the issue. Close an incident after a reproducible test passes, affected pursuits are reconciled, and the revised procedure has a clear owner rather than after an error message disappears.

callout.title: Four pre-flight verifications before publishing a pursuit recommendation
callout.body: A passed technical job is insufficient. The capture lead records these four checks against the specific pursuit.
items: Verify the current solicitation packet, every located amendment, the operative deadline and timezone, and the designated submission channel directly against the issuing source.
Verify the proposed prime's identity, relevant registration and certification evidence, and exclusions findings; investigate potential matches instead of inferring eligibility from a name search.
Verify fee terms, supplier compensation, required workshare, and subcontracting structure against applicable clauses and program rules with the procurement-review contractor.
Verify complete retrieval coverage, acknowledged material changes, supplier quotation validity, and a named backup operator before the recommendation enters the client queue.

sections.heading: 4. Fund the tooling from service economics and protect five-person capacity
paragraphs: Keep Candidate #4's scorecard intact when justifying the stack. Conservative recognized service revenue is $120,000, with a 15% net margin and $18,000 annual owner net profit; implied total annual costs are $102,000. Base revenue is $560,000, with a 22.5% net margin and $126,000 owner profit; implied costs are $434,000. Scaled revenue is $1,000,000, with a 30% net margin and $300,000 owner profit; implied costs are $700,000. Conservative and Base use two full-time employees plus three contractors. Scaled uses three full-time employees plus four contractors, seven people total. Those are canonical cases, not outputs of this chapter's connector design. Client contract ceilings, obligations, subcontract values, and supplier invoices never become desk revenue merely because the pipeline tracks them. Recognize only the desk's earned service fees under its actual engagement terms. The supplied monthly operating-expense range of $5,000 to $25,000 is a planning range, not a substitute for each case's complete annual cost bridge. Separate recurring overhead, direct delivery labor, variable contractor costs, and other expenses so the scorecard's margins reconcile without double counting or pretending that every cost belongs in one monthly overhead bucket.

Evaluate paid intelligence through a bounded test before adding another recurring obligation. An illustrative $400 monthly subscription plus $100 for incremental storage and monitoring totals $6,000 annually; these are desk planning assumptions, not vendor quotations. If verified automation saves ten contractor hours each month at an avoidable $60 hourly cost, the annual benefit is $7,200 and the direct contribution is $1,200 before implementation and review costs. Saved salaried time creates capacity, not automatic cash savings. Count it separately through faster qualified briefs or fewer overdue reviews. Keep this test inside the existing scenario cost envelope; otherwise the published margin must change, so it cannot be presented as the canonical case. Use the $20,000 to $90,000 startup capital range to plan setup and runway against the six-to-eighteen-month time to first deal. Neither range proves that the smallest capital budget covers the longest delay. At $5,000 monthly operating expense, six months already consumes $30,000 before setup costs or additional delivery spending. Favor engagement structures with earned, documented service milestones where appropriate, and review contingent-fee restrictions before linking compensation to awards. A discovery platform cannot cure payment delays or a fee arrangement that the procurement structure does not permit.

Manage the pod through exception volume, not the number of scraped records. The data operator publishes a morning source-health report and a deduplicated change queue. The capture lead reviews deadline and eligibility changes first, then assigns supplier and proposal exceptions to the relevant contractors. Batch lower priority incumbent research into a weekly P2 review. Measure collection freshness, missed amendments, unresolved identity matches, qualified briefs per reviewer hour, supplier quotation expiry, and milestone exceptions. Set internal service targets from actual staffing coverage, distinguishing those targets from agency publication timing and portal availability. Track the fraction of recommendations with complete evidence lineage; a high alert count can hide poor decision quality. Review paid subscriptions monthly against verified decision use, not logins. Retire connectors that produce no actionable evidence, while preserving the authoritative manual fallback. Expand into another municipality only after existing active pursuits have dependable coverage and a tested backup operator. At the Scaled case, assign added capacity to documented bottlenecks such as supplier verification or bid review rather than assuming more sources produce proportionally more fees. The durable advantage is a shorter, auditable path from public evidence to an executable client decision, with supplier failure and payment uncertainty still visible in the operating queue.

chapters.question_prompt: Which federal/state statutes, licensing boundaries, contract clauses, and compliant outreach scripts govern government contract brokering?

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #4, Government Contract Brokering, holds Rank #27 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter organizes execution into seven mapped operator plays: solicitation monitoring, opportunity qualification, bid-calendar control, proposal coordination, prime/sub teaming, supplier readiness, and post-award administration. Sell documented procurement work rather than access to officials or a percentage of public awards. FAR contingent-fee provisions, procurement-integrity restrictions, anti-kickback rules, SBA performance limits, and state purchasing laws shape both scope and compensation. Canonical annual owner net profit is $18,000 Conservative, $126,000 Base, and $300,000 Scaled, on recognized service fees rather than client contract value. A two-employee, three-contractor pod needs explicit decision rights, evidence-backed contracts, and outreach scripts that preserve the buyer's authorized communication channel.

sections.heading: 1. Define Seven Service Plays Before Choosing Any Compensation Formula
paragraphs: Government contract brokering is a commercial label, not a federal license category or permission to sell influence. For Candidate #4, use seven explicit operating plays: P1 solicitation monitoring, P2 opportunity qualification, P3 bid-calendar control, P4 proposal coordination, P5 prime/sub teaming, P6 supplier readiness, and P7 post-award administration. P1 produces a sourced alert; P2 produces a documented bid decision; P3 maintains amendment deadlines; P4 assembles client-approved submissions; P5 documents actual work allocation; P6 verifies supplier capacity; and P7 tracks contractual deliverables and invoice evidence. Each play needs its own acceptance test and accountable employee. The two full-time roles are a managing procurement lead and a bid-operations lead. Three contractors provide proposal production, sector-specific supplier analysis, and specialist contract review under defined work orders. Contractors do not gain authority to certify client representations, promise awards, or contact restricted officials merely by joining the pod. Configure SAM.gov saved searches and a shared calendar before buying expensive databases. Keep the solicitation identifier, amendment version, source URL, retrieval date, and assigned reviewer with every opportunity. These records turn a vague introduction business into auditable service delivery, while exposing work that would exceed the pod's available capacity before a client signs.

Compensation must survive the actual solicitation and the governing rules, not merely carry a consulting label. FAR Subpart 3.4 and FAR 52.203-5 address contingent fees for soliciting or obtaining government contracts, subject to their coverage and bona fide employee or agency exceptions. FAR 3.404 prescribes the covenant for contracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, except commercial products or commercial services; other restrictions can still apply outside that prescription. A payment triggered only by award can remain contingent even when described as a completion bonus. Conversely, an ordinary fixed retainer does not excuse improper influence, unlawful lobbying, or prohibited access. Default to monthly fees for enumerated monitoring work and fixed milestones for completed proposal packages, payable independently of award. Have the specialist review any exception claim against FAR 3.401 and the documented relationship before offering it. Under 31 U.S.C. 1352, covered federal funds cannot pay for specified lobbying activities; disclosure requirements can also attach to payments from other sources. Separate procurement administration from efforts to influence covered officials, and examine lobbying registration obligations independently. The contract must describe real services, real records, and the exact event creating an earned fee.

Treat protected information and supplier compensation as separate risk controls. The procurement-integrity provisions in 41 U.S.C. 2101-2107 and FAR 3.104 restrict knowingly obtaining or disclosing covered contractor bid, proposal, and source-selection information before award. A former official's familiarity with a program does not authorize delivery of a competitor's pricing or an evaluator's private notes. Public amendments, published questions, and authorized market research belong in the workroom; suspicious nonpublic evaluation material belongs in a restricted incident process without further circulation. The Anti-Kickback Act, 41 U.S.C. 8701-8707, reaches things of value provided to improperly obtain or reward favorable treatment involving covered prime contracts or subcontracts. Do not pay a prime's purchasing employee personally for selecting a supplier, and do not route that payment through a marketing invoice. Require written disclosure of referral arrangements, supplier-side compensation, familial interests, and ownership ties before P5 begins. The procurement lead decides whether the engagement can proceed after specialist review; the analyst cannot resolve a conflict by adding a spreadsheet note. Keep separate client workspaces and access logs so competing bidders never share draft prices, strategies, or proposal personnel without a specifically assessed, authorized arrangement.

callout.title: Earn Fees for Evidence, Not Supposed Access
callout.body: Experienced bid desks separate public-source intelligence, authorized client materials, and restricted incident records before a deadline makes shortcuts attractive.
items: Attach the exact amendment identifier to every compliance checklist; a correct answer to an obsolete solicitation still loses.
Ask the client for the solicitation's incorporated clauses before quoting P5 teaming work; the notice summary rarely resolves compensation restrictions.
Invoice P4 against a versioned deliverable manifest, not an award announcement; acceptance evidence should exist even after an unsuccessful bid.
Require supplier referral terms in writing before introductions, then test improper-purpose and conflict risks rather than assuming disclosure cures them.

sections.heading: 2. Recheck State, Sector, and Small-Business Boundaries for Every Opportunity
paragraphs: Build a jurisdiction sheet for each buyer instead of treating SAM.gov familiarity as nationwide authorization. Record whether the purchaser is a federal agency, state entity, municipality, authority, or recipient spending federal assistance. Federal grant procurement can implicate 2 CFR 200.318-200.327 without turning a municipal purchase into a FAR procurement. Add the solicitation's communication restrictions, lobbying rules, vendor registration steps, professional licensing requirements, and public-records procedures. New York State Finance Law sections 139-j and 139-k establish restricted-period contact and disclosure requirements for covered governmental procurements; route communications through designated contacts and document permitted exceptions. Florida Statutes section 287.055 governs covered professional services and includes a contingent-fee prohibition with stated exceptions. Texas Government Code Chapter 2254 uses qualifications-based selection for specified professional services, making a generic lowest-price pitch the wrong operating model. California Public Contract Code section 4104 requires listed subcontractor information in covered public works bids. The point is not to memorize fifty summaries. It is to attach the governing text and buyer instructions to P2 before committing P4 hours or P5 introductions, then assign one reviewer to resolve every identified mismatch.

There is no single federal procurement-broker credential that authorizes engineering, construction, insurance placement, freight brokerage, or other separately regulated services. A bid desk can coordinate a licensed engineer's submission without representing that it offers engineering itself. If the desk begins selling the regulated service, controlling its delivery, or acting as the contracting provider, recheck the applicable firm and individual licensing requirements before accepting that scope. For interstate motor-carrier brokerage, examine 49 U.S.C. 13904 and 13906 alongside the proposed transportation role; ordinary supplier research does not itself establish that role. For public works, inspect contractor licensing, bonding, prevailing-wage provisions, and subcontractor listing requirements. Federal construction may implicate the Davis-Bacon provisions at 40 U.S.C. 3141-3148; covered federal service contracts may implicate 41 U.S.C. Chapter 67. P6 should collect current licenses, insurance evidence, capacity commitments, and applicable wage classifications without pretending those documents prove complete eligibility. Where controlled information or defense clauses appear, identify the actual security requirements before collecting files. Do not put controlled client material into an ordinary shared drive or drafting service merely because the vendor advertises encryption.

Teaming must allocate performance, not manufacture the appearance of an eligible prime. Under 13 CFR 125.6, covered service set-asides generally limit payments to subcontractors that are not similarly situated to fifty percent of the amount paid by the government for contract performance, subject to applicable exclusions and details. Supply and construction categories use different calculations; never reuse the service worksheet without classifying the requirement. Similarly situated status depends on the relevant program status and size under the assigned subcontract NAICS code, not a friendly supplier's assertion that it is small. Also examine the ostensible-subcontractor rule in 13 CFR 121.103 where applicable: an eligible-looking prime can create affiliation risk through unusual reliance on another firm or its performance of primary and vital requirements. FAR 9.6 recognizes contractor team arrangements but does not excuse these restrictions or promise that a teaming memorandum will become an enforceable subcontract. Specify tasks, personnel, supervision, payment responsibility, and replacement rights before pricing. Candidate #4 should normally sell coordination services rather than become a hollow prime. If a client requests a different structure, pause that structure while the pod continues permissible monitoring and document work.

callout.title: Four Checks Before Any Submission or Teaming Commitment
callout.body: The procurement lead records the decision and supporting documents. An unresolved item blocks the affected commitment, not unrelated authorized research.
items: Verify buyer jurisdiction, funding source, current solicitation amendments, designated contacts, and the exact service requiring any license.
Verify compensation triggers against applicable contingent-fee terms, lobbying restrictions, supplier payments, and disclosed conflicts.

sections.heading: 3. Contract for Deliverables and Reconcile Fees to the Canonical Economics
paragraphs: Use a master services agreement with opportunity-specific work orders rather than a broad promise to obtain government business. The scope schedule should identify which of P1 through P7 are purchased, which client inputs are required, and what constitutes a completed output. For P4, completion might require a populated compliance matrix, assembled narrative, attachment inventory, and client review copy; it should not silently include authority to sign certifications or submit through the client's account. Give the client a defined review period and objective correction procedure. Tie the fee to accepted services or clearly described availability, with deposits treated according to the applicable accounting policy rather than automatically as earned revenue. State how amendments, cancellations, protests, and shortened deadlines affect work already performed. Anti-circumvention language should protect identified introductions and legitimate unpaid services for a bounded period, not create an indefinite ownership claim over public opportunities. It must not resurrect a prohibited award commission through liquidated damages or a termination charge. The specialist should assess enforceability under the chosen state law and replace punitive economics with a defensible measure of actual contracted value and documented loss.

Allocate risk to the party controlling the underlying fact. The client owns its pricing decisions, eligibility representations, performance promises, and certification accuracy; the desk owns its agreed process and deliverable obligations. A liability cap might reference fees paid during a defined period, with expressly negotiated treatment of confidentiality breaches, intellectual property claims, intentional misconduct, and other exceptions. Private limitations do not extinguish statutory exposure, and states differ on enforceability. Define escalation, governing law, venue or arbitration, interim relief, collection expenses, and whether work pauses during a payment dispute. Do not confuse this private service dispute process with a bid protest, an agency claim, or the prime's Contract Disputes Act procedures. For intellectual property, distinguish preexisting templates from client-owned bid content and licensed third-party material. For data, identify authorized users, approved storage, incident notice timing, return or deletion procedures, and legally required retention. Government data-rights and security clauses require separate flowdown analysis when applicable. Do not promise that marking every document confidential defeats public-records laws. Finally, require written change orders when P7 expands from tracking invoices into managing performance, accepting deliverables, or directing subcontractors; those activities create materially different responsibility.

Keep the scorecard anchored to recognized service fees. The Conservative case is $120,000 revenue less $102,000 total costs, leaving $18,000 owner net profit at fifteen percent. Base is $560,000 less $434,000, leaving $126,000 at 22.5 percent. Scaled is $1,000,000 less $700,000, leaving $300,000 at thirty percent. An illustrative Base mix is eight clients paying $4,000 monthly for twelve months, producing $384,000, plus twenty-two completed proposal packages at $8,000, producing $176,000. Those packages must be incremental services, not retainer work billed twice. The client's award value and subcontract purchasing spend are excluded from this desk's service-fee revenue. Conservative and Base use two full-time employees plus three contractors; Scaled uses three full-time employees plus four contractors. These are canonical staffing assumptions, not proof that local compensation fits the cost envelope. The Conservative cost allowance is especially tight for that staffing pattern and needs a priced labor plan. The stated $5,000-$25,000 monthly operating range must be reconciled with variable delivery costs rather than substituted for total annual expenses. Budget $20,000-$90,000 startup capital against the six-to-eighteen-month first-deal window, milestone collections, and payment-delay exposure.

sections.heading: 4. Use Authorized Outreach Scripts and a Four-Step Evidence Workflow
paragraphs: Start contractor outreach with a service proposition that can be delivered without privileged access. Use this script verbatim: 'Hello, I run a procurement support desk that monitors public solicitations, controls bid calendars, and assembles client-approved proposal packages. We charge for defined services, not introductions to officials or promised awards. Are you the person responsible for deciding which government opportunities your company pursues? If so, may we schedule a short discussion about your target buyers, delivery capacity, and current bidding process? If this is irrelevant, reply stop and we will suppress further marketing to this address.' Add a truthful sender identity, descriptive subject line, commercial identification where required, and the business's valid physical postal address. CAN-SPAM, 15 U.S.C. 7704, applies to covered commercial email, including business recipients; honor opt-outs within ten business days and supervise any outreach vendor. Do not scrape restricted bidder portals, impersonate a purchasing office, or imply government endorsement. For automated calls or texts, assess 47 U.S.C. 227, implementing FCC rules, and relevant state requirements before using the channel. A public business listing does not by itself authorize every dialing method or destination.

Discovery should establish operational fit before anyone quotes a percentage. Use this script: 'Which legal entity would bid, and who can authorize its representations? Which agencies, municipalities, NAICS codes, and service territories match work you already perform? What licenses, certifications, past-performance records, staffing, insurance, and working capital can you document? Which tasks will your employees perform, and which suppliers would perform the rest? Are there referral payments, competing bidder relationships, former-official relationships, or restricted information we should identify before accepting the engagement? Our next step is a written qualification worksheet and priced service scope, not an award prediction.' Capture answers as client statements until verified, and assign missing evidence to a named owner with a date. For supplier discussions, use: 'We are coordinating a possible bid for a client. Please confirm your proposed work, delivery capacity, license status, price validity, and any conflicts. No award or subcontract is committed by this conversation; any commitment requires authorized written terms.' This separates P2 qualification from P5 promises and gives P6 a usable checklist. Reject requests to backdate commitments, lend an eligibility label, or fabricate project references even when the submission deadline is hours away.

Government-facing outreach must follow the solicitation's channel and timing. Use this script only when that channel permits the contact: 'We support a prospective offeror reviewing the published solicitation. Please confirm the designated process for submitting clarification questions and receiving public amendments. We are not requesting competitor information or evaluation deliberations. Our technical question concerns the stated deliverable and will be submitted through the published channel by the stated deadline.' For pre-solicitation market research, identify the client and purpose accurately, then ask whether capability materials are being accepted. FAR 15.201 encourages appropriate exchanges, but it does not authorize private access to protected information or override procurement-specific instructions. Log the recipient, client authorization, exact message, response, and any required follow-up. The bid lead owns the shared deadline calendar; the procurement lead owns conflicts and exceptions; the three contractors receive task-specific access rather than the entire client portfolio. Automate alerts, calendar reminders, and checklist completeness checks, while retaining human review of eligibility and certifications. At Scaled, add the third employee and fourth contractor to support review capacity, not indiscriminate outreach. Measure overdue questions, amendment acknowledgment, delivery acceptance, and receivable age before increasing opportunity volume.

sop_steps.title: Open a jurisdiction and authority record
sop_steps.action: Assign the procurement lead to identify buyer, funding source, clauses, and authorized contacts.
sop_steps.detail: Attach current solicitation versions, state purchasing requirements, licensing checks, and the client's written authority before contractors receive substantive work.

sop_steps.title: Review compensation and performance structure
sop_steps.action: Route fees, conflicts, set-aside calculations, and supplier arrangements to the specialist reviewer.
sop_steps.detail: Record the governing rule and resulting decision for each affected play; revise prohibited structures without stopping unrelated authorized research.

sop_steps.title: Execute scoped services and controlled communications
sop_steps.action: Have the bid lead issue work orders, approved scripts, calendar assignments, and access permissions.
sop_steps.detail: The client retains certification authority. Every submission package includes an amendment check, deliverable manifest, and documented client review.

sop_steps.title: Close delivery evidence and reconcile service revenue
sop_steps.action: Record acceptance, earned fees, receivables, supplier exceptions, and retention obligations.
sop_steps.detail: Exclude client award value from desk revenue, reconcile costs to the canonical scenario, and revoke access when each contractor's assignment ends.

chapters.pull_quote: Sell a documented procurement process, never a promise that public money will follow an introduction.
action_checklist: Create a seven-play service catalog with deliverables, acceptance tests, client dependencies, and an assigned employee owner for every play.
Attach a jurisdiction sheet, current solicitation clauses, designated-contact rules, and required licensing evidence to each qualified opportunity.
Replace award-dependent compensation with documented service milestones unless specialist review establishes an applicable lawful exception.
Verify prime eligibility, actual subcontract workshare, supplier capacity, similarly situated status, and any applicable product-sourcing requirements.
Execute scope, fee, anti-circumvention, liability, dispute, intellectual-property, and data provisions before sending authorized outreach.
Reconcile recognized fees and total costs to $18,000, $126,000, or $300,000 canonical annual owner net profit without counting client awards as desk revenue.

chapters.question_prompt: How does a 2 FT + 3 C (5 people) government contract brokering team automate 70%+ of repetitive research, qualification, fulfillment, and traffic/deal acquisition while keeping human-in-the-loop QA?
chapters.title: Automation, AI Leverage & Scalable Distribution Flywheels
chapters.subtitle: Build a Python Bid Desk Across SAM.gov, Municipal Portals, FAR Controls, Evidence Queues, and Permissioned Partner Distribution
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #4, Government Contract Brokering, ranks #27 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: a high-leverage operator play, not an autonomous award machine. This chapter maps seven operating plays: solicitation intelligence, qualification, lawful teaming, bid production, fulfillment evidence, service-fee collections, and partner distribution. A 2 FT + 3 C pod uses Python ingestion, authenticated webhooks, evidence-linked LLM extraction, and exception queues to target 70%+ automation of measured repetitive work while people retain consequential decisions. Recognized service fees support annual owner profit of $18,000 Conservative, $126,000 Base, and $300,000 Scaled; the Scaled case requires 3 FT + 4 C. The operating advantage comes from reusable evidence and trustworthy distribution, not procurement shortcuts or counting client awards as revenue.

sections.heading: 1. Turn seven operating plays into one evidence-linked work queue
paragraphs: Design the desk around seven mapped operating plays rather than seven disconnected software subscriptions. The chapter's operational mapping is solicitation intelligence, qualification, lawful teaming, bid production, fulfillment evidence, service-fee collections, and partner distribution; these labels organize delivery without adding new scorecard assumptions. Assign the first full-time person as capture lead and the second as operations lead. Allocate the three contractors to procurement review, proposal production, and supplier verification, with purchased hours and backup coverage recorded explicitly. Contractor headcount does not mean unlimited availability. Every opportunity receives a stable identifier, buyer, jurisdiction, notice type, solicitation number, source URL, retrieval timestamp, document digest, deadline, assigned reviewer, and next action. Keep opportunity records separate from client engagements and supplier records: one procurement can produce several client discussions but should never become several supposed awards. Use SQLite for a single-writer pilot and a managed relational store when concurrent workers justify migration. A shared queue, not a chat transcript, determines ownership. The capture lead owns pursuit decisions; the operations lead owns queue health and evidence completeness. This division keeps the five-person pod from silently delegating binding commitments to whichever contractor happens to receive an alert.

Build the ingestion worker with Python urllib.request, json, hashlib, sqlite3, and zoneinfo. Query the SAM.gov Opportunities API using documented filters, pagination, and account-specific limits; obtain credentials through the operator's authorized account and keep them outside prompts and logs. Treat municipal Bonfire, OpenGov Procurement, and BidNet Direct feeds as separate connectors because access methods and attachment permissions vary. Where no authorized machine interface exists, route portal email into a review inbox and let a person retrieve restricted material. Never bypass authentication to improve coverage. Store each original document before extracting fields, then deduplicate on jurisdiction, solicitation identifier, and document digest rather than title alone. A changed digest creates an amendment event even when the title remains identical. Polling workers emit versioned events into an outbox; a dispatcher posts them to the calendar and task service using authenticated webhooks. Validate provider signatures, reject stale delivery timestamps, and enforce unique event identifiers. Persist the event before acknowledging delivery so a process restart cannot erase an amendment. Limit document size and isolate parsing because public procurement attachments remain untrusted input.

Measure the 70%+ target against repetitive labor minutes, not total headcount, award dollars, or the percentage of records touched by software. Establish a matched baseline across research, qualification preparation, fulfillment evidence indexing, and acquisition-list preparation. In an illustrative sample, those tasks previously consumed 1,000 active minutes; automation removes 780 minutes but introduces 60 minutes of exception handling, leaving 280 minutes and a 72% net reduction. Count the exception minutes even when contractors perform them. Keep final bid approval, supplier judgment, and client commitments outside the automation claim unless their actual repetitive components were separately timed. Instrument each run with task category, source version, outcome, reviewer minutes, and correction reason. Compare similar document lengths and notice types so an easy week does not masquerade as a productivity gain. Require stable results across four weekly samples before changing staffing assumptions. A sample that saves 650 minutes after rework supports 65%, and the dashboard must say so. Use the recovered capacity for additional qualified pursuits and faster amendment reviews before promising more clients. The seven-play design scales only when each additional pursuit has an accountable human owner.

sections.heading: 2. Use LLMs for evidence extraction while people control procurement representations
paragraphs: Place the LLM behind a narrow extraction contract rather than giving it authority over the bid desk. Supply public solicitation text, an explicit field schema, and instructions to return source excerpts for every consequential assertion. Procurement attachments can contain malicious instructions or merely confusing boilerplate; treat both as document content, never as executable directions. The model receives no portal password, signing authority, or ability to email a contracting officer. Validate JSON types, allowable enumerations, deadline syntax, and excerpt presence before displaying results. Preserve the distinction between a requirement, an evaluation factor, an optional attachment, and background narrative. A missing performance location should create a reviewer task, not a plausible location invented from the agency address. Use deterministic checks for attachment counts and required forms, then reserve model work for clause classification and cross-document comparison. Benchmark the extractor on a frozen set of reviewed solicitations containing amendments, scanned schedules, and conflicting dates. Track false clearances separately from harmless extra review tasks: declaring a bidder eligible when evidence is absent is more costly than asking a reviewer to inspect an additional page.

Qualification must test the proposed transaction, not simply find the word subcontractor. FAR 52.203-5 restricts contingent-fee arrangements where the clause applies, subject to its defined exceptions; labeling a success payment a consulting retainer does not change its substance. Prefer documented fees for actual research, proposal, and administration services, and have the procurement reviewer examine compensation structure before engagement. Procurement integrity under 41 U.S.C. 2102 and FAR 3.104 requires rejecting protected bid, proposal, or source-selection information received outside authorized channels. Anti-kickback controls under 41 U.S.C. 8702 require scrutiny of supplier referral payments, gifts, and credits intended to obtain or reward favorable treatment. For covered set-asides, evaluate FAR 52.219-14 by contract category and the treatment of similarly situated entities; do not apply one universal subcontracting percentage. Where applicable, FAR 52.215-23 addresses excessive pass-through charges, making an empty intermediary structure especially fragile. Municipal work requires its own ordinance and solicitation review rather than an assumption that federal clauses govern. Automation assembles these questions with citations; the reviewer resolves applicability, and the authorized prime signs its own representations.

Make the bid calendar a dependency graph with explicit evidence locks. An amendment affecting delivery dates should reopen supplier availability, pricing validity, staffing assumptions, and the draft schedule instead of merely changing a calendar entry. Generate internal reminders at seven days, three days, and one day when the procurement timeline permits, with an earlier cutoff for uploads requiring large attachments. Capture the solicitation's actual submission mechanism: portal upload, sealed package, and authorized email are different workflows. The proposal contractor can assemble a checklist from reviewed clauses, but the capture lead verifies every required attachment, signature, acknowledgment, and price schedule against the latest source version. Require supplier quotations to identify scope, exclusions, validity period, lead time, and the person authorized to commit resources. No model-generated capability statement becomes a factual claim without supporting evidence. For restricted client material, use only processing environments approved for that data category and contractual obligations; otherwise keep extraction local or manual. The final submission remains a deliberate human action, followed by receipt capture and an independent check that the submitted files match the approved package.

sections.heading: 3. Price automated runs and recover failures without breaking the scorecard
paragraphs: Price an automated run as a bounded document-processing attempt, not an entire successful procurement. For an illustrative planning rate, 6,000 input tokens at $2 per million cost $0.012, and 1,500 output tokens at $12 per million cost $0.018. Add $0.020 for allocated compute, storage, and event delivery plus a $0.010 retry reserve: total direct cost is $0.060 per run. These are budgeting assumptions rather than a vendor quote; substitute the contracted model tariff and measured token usage before purchasing capacity. At 3,000 runs monthly, direct processing costs $180. If 90 runs require eight minutes of exception review at a loaded $60 hourly rate, that review costs $720, producing $900 combined expense or $0.30 per run. Final bid reviews, software subscriptions, connector maintenance, ordinary fulfillment labor, and sales work remain additional expenses. Log those costs separately to prevent a cheap extraction metric from concealing an expensive desk. Route long documents through section selection and digest-based caching, but invalidate cached decisions when relevant source content changes. Cost controls must never suppress a material amendment merely because the monthly token budget is nearly spent.

Reconcile the operating model to recognized service fees, not the face value of client awards. Conservative revenue is $120,000 at a 15% net margin, leaving $18,000 annual owner net profit and $102,000 implied annual expenses. Base revenue is $560,000 at 22.5%, leaving $126,000 profit and $434,000 expenses. Scaled revenue is $1,000,000 at 30%, leaving $300,000 profit and $700,000 expenses. Illustrative fee arithmetic is twelve $10,000 completed service packages, twenty-eight $20,000 packages, and forty $25,000 packages respectively; actual recognition follows the engagement's earned-service terms, not invoice issuance alone. These are alternative annual scenarios, not additive revenue streams. Conservative and Base retain 2 FT + 3 C; Scaled requires 3 FT + 4 C. The Conservative expense ceiling is tight for that staffing label, so explicitly budget compensation, contractor hours, and owner labor rather than pretending headcount establishes affordability. The stated $5,000–$25,000 monthly operating range is a planning envelope, not permission to exclude delivery labor from scenario expenses. Startup capital of $20,000–$90,000 and a 6–18 month first-deal window demand a separate cash runway schedule before hiring or committing to annual software contracts.

Fulfillment automation begins after scope and responsibility are settled. Create an evidence register for supplier milestones, inspection records, delivery confirmations, client acceptance, and the service desk's own completed work. Keep client goods and subcontractor obligations separate from the operator's service-fee ledger. The collections play drafts invoices from reviewed milestones, reconciles receipts, and alerts the operations lead to disputes; it does not charge clients for a model's unsupported completion inference. Federal prompt-payment rules do not automatically determine when a private client owes this desk, so monitor the actual engagement terms and cash aging. Supplier failure requires a named escalation path, documented alternatives, and buyer or prime authorization where changes require it. For technical failures, set connector timeouts, bounded retries, and a circuit breaker that stops repeated processing of a corrupt attachment. Preserve a daily export of active pursuits, deadlines, and evidence links so the pod can operate manually during an outage. Restore from tested backups, replay idempotent events, and reconcile every external action before restarting automatic dispatch. A recovered database is insufficient if the calendar still contains superseded deadlines or invoices were transmitted twice.

sections.heading: 4. Build distribution loops from reviewed procurement intelligence
paragraphs: Build programmatic distribution from the same reviewed opportunity records used by the desk, but publish a deliberately smaller public dataset. A useful page serves a specific buyer problem: municipal facilities maintenance bids in one region, upcoming federal laboratory supply opportunities, or a supplier-readiness checklist for one contract category. Include authoritative links, last-checked timestamps, closing dates, and a clear explanation of what the service desk actually provides. Do not republish client pricing, restricted attachments, or another bidder's capability evidence. Generate drafts automatically, then have the capture lead approve substantive pages before first publication and material revisions. Expire closed notices visibly and distinguish opportunity summaries from official government instructions. Thin location pages containing identical text will not create a durable acquisition advantage. Instead, combine verified local portal coverage with original comparisons of submission mechanics and supplier preparation requirements. Track indexed pages, qualified inquiries, accepted engagements, and earned fees by source. Impressions are diagnostic, not revenue. One accurate niche page that generates a service-ready client can outperform hundreds of automatically published pages that attract suppliers unable to meet the underlying requirements.

Create a permissioned sharing loop around supplier usefulness rather than promised influence. After a reviewed shortlist is delivered, offer the recipient a shareable public digest and a separate invitation link for colleagues who want future notices. The recipient chooses whether to share; the system never uploads their address book. Attribute referrals with campaign identifiers that reveal no private client relationship. Partner with relevant APEX Accelerators, trade associations, and complementary proposal specialists through educational resources and transparent service descriptions; never imply government endorsement. For commercial outbound email, use accurate headers and subjects, identify the sender, provide a valid postal address and working opt-out, and honor suppression requirements under 15 U.S.C. 7704. Screen business contacts against the desk's suppression list before any send. Keep outreach specific: identify the public notice, explain a documented capability fit, and invite a conversation rather than asserting award likelihood. The capture lead approves recipient criteria and message templates before dispatch. Referral compensation requires the same contingent-fee and anti-kickback analysis as other compensation; a marketing label does not remove procurement risk.

Close the flywheel with evidence from delivery, not vanity engagement. A completed qualification checklist improves the next supplier intake; an amendment postmortem improves the extraction test set; an accepted service milestone supports a client-approved case study; a helpful public digest attracts another properly matched supplier. These connections join all seven plays without granting software independent authority to pursue, certify, submit, or commit resources. Run a weekly forty-five-minute pod review covering feed freshness, disputed deadlines, false clearances, supplier exceptions, unpaid service fees, and acquisition quality. Give each defect one owner and one measurable repair. Track qualified-lead conversion and service contribution by channel, then throttle distribution when the human review queue exceeds capacity. For example, stop new campaign sends when unresolved material amendments threaten active submissions; keep essential client notifications running. Add the Scaled case's third full-time person and fourth contractor only after earned service demand and cash coverage support that capacity. The durable advantage is a growing library of verified requirements, capable suppliers, and trustworthy operating evidence, not a larger pile of unreviewed model output.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 2 FT + 3 C (5 people) -> 3 FT + 4 C (7 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?
chapters.title: Pod Architecture, Contractor KPIs & Exit Valuation
chapters.subtitle: SAM.gov Bid-Desk Seats, FAR-Aware Teaming, Weekly Contractor Scorecards, Accrual Cohorts & Transferable Service-Fee Earnings
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #4, Government Contract Brokering, ranks #27 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Build its procurement-services business around seven mapped operator plays: solicitation intelligence, opportunity qualification, bid-calendar control, proposal assembly, teaming diligence, submission quality assurance, and post-award coordination. Two full-time seats and three contractors support the Conservative and Base cases; three full-time seats and four contractors support Scaled operations. Canonical annual owner profits are $18,000, $126,000, and $300,000, respectively. This chapter converts those staffing limits into accountable seats, purchased contractor capacity, weekly evidence-backed metrics, concentration limits, and transferable records. Recognize service fees rather than client award values, price founder replacement before discussing multiples, and preserve a cash-generating operating option when acquisition terms disappoint.

key_metrics.label: Conservative
key_metrics.context: Annual recognized procurement-service fees, excluding client contract awards
key_metrics.note: 15% net margin; $18,000 annual owner net profit; 2 FT + 3 C

key_metrics.label: Base
key_metrics.context: Annual recognized procurement-service fees, excluding client contract awards
key_metrics.note: 22.5% net margin; $126,000 annual owner net profit; 2 FT + 3 C

sections.heading: 1. Assign seven operator plays to five accountable seats
paragraphs: Define the business as a procurement-services desk, not an award-resale machine. For this chapter, map its seven operator plays as P1 solicitation intelligence, P2 opportunity qualification, P3 bid-calendar control, P4 proposal assembly, P5 teaming diligence, P6 submission quality assurance, and P7 post-award coordination. These are operating workstreams, not seven additional revenue assumptions. In the five-person pod, FT1 is the principal and account lead, accountable for P2, P5, client scope, pricing, and cash collection. FT2 is the delivery manager, accountable for P3, P6, workload sequencing, and acceptance evidence. Contractor C1 performs P1 research and qualification preparation; C2 produces P4 response packages; C3 supplies specialist reviews and P7 administrative support. Each play has one accountable employee even when several people contribute. The client retains responsibility for its representations, pricing decisions, and authorized submission signatures. Use SAM.gov saved searches, agency acquisition forecasts, and the actual municipal purchasing portal as source systems. Record the solicitation identifier, amendment number, source URL, due time, and time zone before work enters the queue. A notification email is merely a lead; the controlling solicitation and amendments define the deliverable. Assign a backup employee to every deadline so principal absence does not suspend service.

Purchase contractor outputs and reserved capacity rather than pretending three contractors equal three full-time employees. An illustrative Base budget buys 720 annual research hours at $45, 720 proposal hours at $65, and 320 specialist hours at $90: $32,400 plus $46,800 plus $28,800 equals $108,000. That is 1,760 purchased hours across three people, with surge work requiring an explicit scope adjustment. These rates are planning inputs, not market quotations. Contracts specify deliverable format, source traceability, revision boundaries, confidentiality, conflict disclosure, and a signed assignment of copyright under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a). Do not rely solely on work-made-for-hire wording for commissioned materials. Require research delivery within two business days of assignment, proposal drafts three business days before the internal cutoff, and specialist review within one business day after a complete package arrives. Reserve review capacity when accepting the assignment; an SLA without capacity is fiction. Pay accepted hourly work or defined milestones, never a routine percentage of federal awards. Apply FAR Subpart 3.4 to contingent-fee arrangements, including the facts supporting any applicable exception. Independence must also be genuine: output specifications do not cure worker misclassification when actual control and economic dependence point toward employment.

Add the seventh-person configuration only when measured workload supports it. FT3 becomes the account-operations lead, taking P7 and recurring client reporting from FT1; C4 provides independent proposal review and amendment coverage under FT2. The resulting three full-time seats and four contractors remain seven people, not seven unrestricted production equivalents. Keep authors and final reviewers separate on every material submission, including municipal responses with different procurement codes. Use SharePoint version history for controlled documents and an Asana board for owners, dependencies, and internal cutoffs; neither replaces the government portal receipt. Track client permission for credentials and signatures, and avoid shared personal accounts. Before proposing prime/sub arrangements, check the actual solicitation, applicable FAR 52.219-14 clause, and 13 CFR 125.6 limitations on subcontracting. Review ostensible-subcontractor exposure under 13 CFR 121.103 where relevant. A bid desk cannot manufacture eligibility by placing a nominal qualifying firm above the real performer. Treat supplier capability as evidence-based: staff availability, relevant past performance, required licenses, and signed commitments. The pod sells coordination and execution discipline; it does not sell access to officials. Procurement-integrity and anti-kickback requirements apply to conduct regardless of whether the business calls itself a broker, consultant, or teaming adviser.

callout.title: Protect scarce reviewer hours before chasing more solicitations
callout.body: The practical constraint is usually reliable review capacity near clustered deadlines, not the number of searchable opportunities.
items: Reserve a named reviewer when opening each pursuit; never discover review demand on submission morning.
Save the solicitation and every amendment with retrieval timestamps; email alerts can arrive after material changes.
Price municipal portal registration and upload rehearsal as explicit scope when the client lacks working credentials.
Give contractor invoices the same client, pursuit, and play codes used in the margin ledger so overruns remain traceable.

sections.heading: 2. Run a weekly scorecard that rewards accepted work and collected fees
paragraphs: Run a forty-five-minute Monday operating review from a frozen Friday dataset. FT2 publishes the queue; FT1 resolves scope and collection decisions. Score P1 on qualified opportunities accepted by FT1, not scraped notice volume. Score P2 on documented bid/no-bid decisions before production begins. Score P3 on amendments incorporated before internal cutoffs, and P4 on first-pass acceptance of complete response packages. Score P5 on verified supplier commitments and unresolved eligibility issues, P6 on accepted submissions with portal receipts, and P7 on timely client reports and resolved invoice exceptions. Define first-pass acceptance as packages accepted without material correction divided by packages reviewed that week. A material correction changes eligibility, pricing, required evidence, or responsiveness; a stylistic edit does not. Start with a 95% first-pass target and zero missed external deadlines, then inspect the underlying cases instead of rewarding denominator manipulation. Record sample sizes beside every percentage. One accepted package out of one is not evidence of stable quality. Track award outcomes separately by solicitation cohort, because agencies control evaluation schedules and award decisions. Never dock a contractor simply because a fully responsive client lost on price. Use debrief findings to improve qualification rather than rewriting the historical submission score.

Convert the weekly board into capacity decisions. For each seat, divide committed production and review hours over the next fourteen days by available contracted hours over that same window. Treat utilization above 85% as a planning warning, not a universal productivity benchmark; the remaining capacity absorbs amendments, client delays, and portal failures. A yellow condition prompts scope resequencing, while a predicted missed external deadline requires immediate principal intervention. Contractor QA uses a written defect taxonomy: critical defects include wrong offeror identity, unsupported certification, omitted mandatory attachment, or unauthorized disclosure; major defects include broken cross-references or inconsistent pricing schedules. Critical defects trigger package isolation and independent reinspection before submission. Require defect acknowledgment within four business hours during agreed coverage, with a correction plan by the next business day. Those are response commitments, not permission to exceed a government deadline. Allocate rework charges according to the contract: contractor error, client scope change, and newly issued amendment are different causes. Maintain a backup reviewer with equivalent access permissions and conflict screening. Do not improve apparent throughput by sending protected procurement material into unapproved software. Tool convenience never substitutes for the client's information-handling requirements or the contract's specific security obligations.

Apply a 25% ceiling to both customer revenue concentration and critical delivery-counterparty dependence. Measure each customer and related customer group against trailing-twelve-month recognized service fees; repeat the calculation on signed forward service backlog to expose pending concentration. Separately measure each critical subcontractor or supplier against delivery spend, and identify indispensable single-source dependencies even when their spend share is small. At the Base case, 25% of $560,000 is $140,000; at Scaled, 25% of $1,000,000 is $250,000. These are customer-fee limits, not caps on the customer's government award value. A young desk may exceed the ceiling before its fourth meaningful account; report that breach plainly, stop expanding the dominant account's exposure, and prioritize diversification rather than disguising related entities as separate customers. Also report exposure by agency, municipal jurisdiction, and prime contractor, since apparently diverse clients can depend on one funding source. Track receivables aging weekly and suspend new discretionary work when contractual payment triggers are breached. Predefine escalation and continuity duties so a collection dispute does not cause an avoidable live-submission failure. Weekly decisions must identify an owner, due date, and measurable closure condition.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile service-fee cohorts to the canonical owner-profit cases
paragraphs: Keep the canonical cases intact: Conservative recognizes $120,000 of service fees, incurs $102,000 of total costs, and leaves $18,000 at 15%; Base recognizes $560,000, incurs $434,000, and leaves $126,000 at 22.5%; Scaled recognizes $1,000,000, incurs $700,000, and leaves $300,000 at 30%. A client's $8 million award contributes zero to desk revenue unless the desk separately earns contracted service fees. Never book that award as brokerage turnover or use it to inflate acquisition metrics. An illustrative Base cost envelope allocates $180,000 to the two employee seats, $108,000 to the three contractor engagements, and $146,000 to remaining delivery and operating costs. A Scaled envelope allocates $300,000 to three employees, $160,000 to four contractors, and $240,000 to remaining costs. These envelopes reconcile arithmetic; they do not establish prevailing compensation. The Conservative $102,000 ceiling is especially tight for two full-time seats plus purchased contractor work. Document actual compensation, owner labor, and deferred economic requirements rather than claiming it funds market-rate replacement staffing. The stated $5,000–$25,000 monthly operating range cannot represent all-in Scaled costs: $700,000 divided by twelve is approximately $58,333 monthly. Separate overhead from total delivery costs when using that planning range.

Close books on accrual principles with client, engagement, play, and origination-cohort codes. Recognize a monthly stand-ready retainer over the service period when that reflects the performance obligation; recognize a discrete proposal milestone when the applicable recognition criteria are satisfied. A deposit received before performance remains a contract liability, not earned revenue. Where ASC 606 applies, document the performance obligations and recognition method with the accountant. Accrue accepted contractor work in the same reporting period as delivery, even if the invoice arrives later. Reconcile QuickBooks Online or Xero project detail to signed scopes, acceptance records, receivables, bank deposits, and contractor commitments. Treat reimbursed costs according to the actual principal-versus-agent analysis, not whichever presentation produces larger revenue. Keep unbilled earned fees separate from conditional opportunities and unperformed backlog. Track bad-debt estimates and credit notes by originating cohort so weak clients do not disappear inside current-month totals. Each month, bridge opening receivables plus invoices minus collections and credits to closing receivables. Then bridge recognized revenue to billings through contract assets and liabilities. An attractive profit statement without those bridges can conceal delayed billing, disputed acceptance, or cash taken for work still owed.

Build cohort reporting around the month the service relationship began, not the government's eventual award month. For each cohort, report opening recurring fees, expansion, contraction, churn, recognized project fees, direct contractor costs, allocated employee delivery time, and cash collected. Keep recurring retainers separate from one-off proposal projects; a client purchasing two bids does not automatically create annual recurring revenue. Measure gross retention only on an identified recurring-fee population, and publish the formula alongside the result. Track proposal margins by complexity band so a simple municipal quote does not subsidize an unpriced federal technical volume indefinitely. Use time records to test the allocation method, including founder hours that are absent from payroll. Model a thirteen-week cash forecast using contractual payment dates and observed collection behavior. A client's government payment expectations do not automatically determine when the desk gets paid. The stated 3–12 months to first deal makes the $20,000–$90,000 startup range a runway constraint, not a hiring instruction. At $25,000 monthly cash burn, $150,000 funds six months before collections or additional capital. Rephase hiring and discretionary spending when signed fees cannot support the projected cash trough.

sections.heading: 4. Price transferable earnings rather than founder-dependent award stories
paragraphs: Prepare a buyer-ready record before requesting a multiple. Assemble signed client scopes, renewal terms, termination rights, assignment provisions, contractor agreements, intellectual-property assignments, monthly accrual statements, cohort bridges, and receipt-backed delivery logs. Separate reusable desk templates from client-owned proposal content and government information subject to handling restrictions. Section 204(a) requires a signed writing for a copyright ownership transfer; an invoice alone does not establish ownership. Inventory any third-party licenses and identify which can transfer. A buyer also needs evidence that account relationships survive the founder: record nonfounder client contacts, renewal ownership, documented workflows, and successful delivery during planned founder absences. Distinguish assignment of ordinary advisory contracts from transfer of an actual federal contract. If the business holds federal contracts, an asset transaction may require novation analysis under FAR 42.1204 and the transfer restrictions in 41 U.S.C. section 6305. Do not promise that a buyer inherits awards, set-aside eligibility, or agency relationships automatically. Where services create organizational conflicts of interest, preserve the FAR Subpart 9.5 analysis and client restrictions. Redact and stage diligence access rather than exposing protected proposal material to every prospective acquirer.

Use valuation ranges as negotiation sensitivities, not reported transaction comparables. For a small owner-operated desk, test roughly 2–3 times properly normalized seller discretionary earnings; for a demonstrably manager-run book, test roughly 3–4 times normalized EBITDA. Those are different denominators and must never be mixed. The canonical owner-profit figures are neither automatically EBITDA nor automatically seller discretionary earnings. Bridge them through actual owner compensation, interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, and supportable adjustments before selecting a valuation basis. For a simplified replacement-adjusted sensitivity, assume the canonical profit includes no compensation for the owner's delivery role, all other normalization adjustments are zero, and that role requires additional fully loaded replacement cost. Base profit of $126,000 less $90,000 then leaves $36,000; a 2.5–3.5 times sensitivity implies $90,000–$126,000 of enterprise value. Scaled profit of $300,000 less $120,000 leaves $180,000; 3–4 times implies $540,000–$720,000. Conservative profit of $18,000 less $90,000 is negative $72,000, so this method supports no positive earnings-based valuation. Do not subtract replacement cost twice when equivalent management compensation is already included in the expense base.

A premium within any negotiated range must come from reduced transfer risk: diversified fees, repeatable retention, current IP assignments, low defect rates, reliable collections, and delivery that does not require founder heroics. Award win rate alone cannot establish durability because the mix of solicitations, client capabilities, and agency budgets changes. Compare offers on cash at close, seller financing, earnout definitions, working-capital adjustments, escrow, and retained liabilities. Enterprise value becomes equity proceeds only after the transaction's cash, debt, and other agreed adjustments; headline price is not distributable cash. For an earnout, define recognized service fees, eligible customers, attribution of renewals, collection conditions, and the buyer's ability to change staffing or pricing. Exclude client award principal from every revenue definition. If offers undervalue dependable distributions, retain the business as a managed cash cow and test quarterly whether the principal can step away without degraded delivery or collections. Keep the same concentration ceilings, replacement-cost analysis, and cash reserves after deciding not to sell. Transferability is useful even without a transaction: it protects continuity during illness, contractor departure, supplier failure, and uneven government procurement cycles.

chapters.question_prompt: What is the exact Day-1-to-Day-30 execution schedule for launching government contract brokering, and what quantitative thresholds govern Kill, Fix, or Scale decisions at Day 30/60/90?
chapters.title: The First 30-Day Launch Sprint & Kill / Fix / Scale Gates
chapters.subtitle: A SAM.gov and Municipal Bid-Desk Sprint: Seven Operator Plays, FAR Teaming Controls, Cash Limits, and Evidence-Based Day 30/60/90 Decisions
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #4, Government Contract Brokering, ranks #27 with a 79/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Launch a paid procurement-services desk, not an award-prediction business. Map seven plays into one controlled workflow: solicitation monitoring, bid qualification, deadline management, proposal assembly, supplier diligence, prime/sub teaming, and invoice administration. The first month proves buyer demand, lawful delivery, and cash discipline using a 2 FT + 3 C pod. Day 30/60/90 decisions use collected service fees, accepted work, contribution margin, and runway rather than advertised contract ceilings. Canonical annual owner profits remain $18,000 Conservative, $126,000 Base, and $300,000 Scaled. The sprint does not compress the stated 6–18-month first-deal horizon; it tests whether customers will pay for useful work before an award arrives.

key_metrics.note: 15% net margin; $18,000 annual owner net profit; 2 FT + 3 C

key_metrics.note: 22.5% net margin; $126,000 annual owner net profit; 2 FT + 3 C

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Build a Lawful, Costed Bid Desk Before Selling Access
paragraphs: Start Day 1 by narrowing Candidate #4 to one buyer problem: help established suppliers decide which public solicitations to pursue and assemble responsive submissions. Select one service category, two federal buying offices, and one municipal portal; janitorial services for nearby facilities is a workable example when the team understands staffing, site visits, and wage determinations. Use SAM.gov Contract Opportunities and the municipality's official procurement website as source records, with USAspending.gov only for historical award research. Map the seven operator plays explicitly: P1 solicitation monitoring, P2 bid qualification, P3 deadline management, P4 proposal assembly, P5 supplier diligence, P6 prime/sub teaming, and P7 invoice administration. These are the sprint's operating labels, not seven separate businesses. Assign each opportunity one source URL, solicitation number, amendment history, customer, owner, and next action. Capture the actual solicitation attachments rather than relying on an alert excerpt. Federal and municipal requirements stay in separate checklists because a FAR provision does not automatically govern a city purchase. By Day 2, the desk must explain precisely which customer work it sells and which contractual responsibilities remain with the bidding prime. Reject requests to sell influence or privileged access.

Keep the initial pod at 2 FT + 3 C: one full-time commercial lead owns discovery, scopes, collections, and customer decisions; one full-time delivery lead owns the bid calendar, source records, and document quality. Three contractors provide proposal editing, supplier costing, and procurement-law review under capped assignments. Budget 80 employee hours and 24 combined contractor hours weekly, with 70 hours reserved for delivery and 34 for selling, administration, and rework. Contractor headcount does not mean three full-time schedules. Measure actual hours by play and customer from the first assignment using Toggl Track or a controlled spreadsheet. Establish Microsoft Lists for the opportunity register, Outlook for deadlines, and SharePoint for versioned workpapers; equivalent tools are acceptable when ownership and audit trails remain clear. Restrict the starter service to public solicitation material and ordinary customer business records. Do not accept controlled unclassified information merely because a customer can upload it. Contract clauses and information categories determine additional system requirements. Reserve review capacity before accepting a rush job, and cap simultaneous submission projects at three until measured touch time supports another. Every client receives a named alternate for deadline coverage.

Before outreach, have the specialist review the compensation model against FAR Subpart 3.4 and FAR 52.203-5 where applicable. Fixed fees for real deliverables reduce dependence on awards but do not excuse influence selling, improper payments, or inaccurate certifications. Examine procurement integrity under 41 U.S.C. 2102 and kickbacks under 41 U.S.C. 8702; document refusal of nonpublic source-selection material and payments intended to secure favorable treatment. For this illustrative launch, authorize $90,000 of available capital, a maximum $20,000 cash outflow in each 30-day period, and a $60,000 cumulative ceiling through Day 90. That leaves a $30,000 reserve before customer collections. The ceiling includes payroll, contractor invoices, tools, insurance, and professional review; it is a limit, not a spending target. Obtain actual payroll and contractor quotes by Day 5. If two full-time roles cannot fit, fund the difference within the ceiling or stop the proposed launch; do not silently replace the specified pod. Maintain a 13-week cash forecast separating unrestricted cash, customer deposits owed against undelivered work, receivables, and committed payments. The minimum ongoing reserve equals eight weeks of forecast net cash burn plus noncancelable obligations falling after that window.
