callout.title: Four Verifications Before Accepting a Customer's First Deadline
callout.body: A signed service order authorizes only its stated scope. Check these four records before accepting money or taking responsibility for a submission milestone.
items: Verify the customer's authorized signer, required bidder registrations, eligibility representations, and responsibility for final certifications; SAM.gov registration itself is free.
Record the compensation review, relevant solicitation clauses, municipal intermediary restrictions, and any unresolved teaming question before offering the affected service.
Confirm the source deadline, time zone, amendment set, required site visits, and designated submission account with an independent second reviewer.
Confirm paid capacity, contractor availability, cash reserve, and a usable delivery environment appropriate to the information actually being handled.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Sell Paid Work Packages, Not the Government's Contract Ceiling
paragraphs: Use Days 8–10 to interview established suppliers rather than cold-pitching public officials for introductions. Build a list of 40 distinct qualified supplier accounts with evidence of relevant delivery capability, an identifiable decision-maker, and a plausible procurement need. Historical award records can identify incumbents and adjacent suppliers, but an old award is neither current demand nor permission to reuse a contact's personal information indiscriminately. A qualified outreach counts once per account after a tailored message reaches a relevant business contact; automated retries do not enlarge the denominator. Ask for the last abandoned bid, estimated preparation hours, supplier-quote failures, and the customer's payment process. Record why they would pay now even if the next award takes months. Target eight completed discovery calls by Day 30, with each call producing a stated problem, a named buyer, a budget discussion, and a dated next step. A polite reply is not discovery. Do not contact officials through prohibited channels once a solicitation restricts communications. Public question periods, industry days, and official clarification procedures are useful research channels, not substitutes for customer willingness to buy. Keep the sales record separate from the government's evaluation or award timeline.

Offer two tightly bounded starter packages. A $2,000 bid-readiness assessment covers one solicitation, an eligibility matrix, a bid/no-bid recommendation, and a calendar; a $4,000 monthly bid-desk retainer covers a defined alert set, weekly reviews, and separately limited document support. These prices are illustrative test offers, not additions to the canonical scorecard. Specify revision limits, customer dependencies, acceptance evidence, payment dates, and excluded representation or certification tasks. Collect an agreed assessment deposit or first retainer installment before reserving delivery hours. Track cash collection independently from recognized revenue: an advance for unfinished work remains a delivery obligation, while completed services are recognized under the operator's consistently applied accounting policy. Never book a $500,000 client award as desk revenue. If the desk earns $4,000 for support, its revenue basis is the earned $4,000 service fee, not the prime's receipts or potential contract ceiling. For unit testing, a completed $2,000 assessment using eight direct hours at a $75 fully loaded rate consumes $600, leaving $1,400, or 70%, before shared overhead. Adding $200 of direct specialist review reduces that contribution to $1,200, or 60%; neither percentage is owner net margin.

Days 11–14 convert interviews into three priced proposals and at least one signed assessment order, with a second paying customer targeted by Day 30. Each proposal maps specific outputs to P1–P7, including plays excluded from that particular purchase. A readiness assessment may use P1–P3 heavily while flagging later supplier and teaming work; do not bill for seven completed services when only three were delivered. Make the commercial lead responsible for the order and collections, the delivery lead responsible for effort estimates, and the editing contractor responsible for a readability check only after substantive requirements are correct. Test the $75 labor assumption against payroll burden and actual contractor rates rather than treating it as an industry benchmark. Use a weekly capacity board showing committed hours, remaining hours, and deadline collisions. No single new customer should consume more than 35 of the pod's 70 delivery hours in a week during this sprint. Price additional work explicitly when an amendment changes the scope. If qualified buyers repeatedly reject the same offer, change the deliverable or segment before buying more lead volume. Procurement software cannot repair a service that customers do not value.

callout.title: Veteran Bid-Desk Tactics That Prevent Expensive False Positives
callout.body: The fastest desk is the one that rejects unsuitable opportunities early and preserves evidence when requirements change.
items: Read amendments before polishing the proposal: changed quantities, wage determinations, or mandatory visits can invalidate yesterday's attractive opportunity.
Ask suppliers for quote expiration, freight assumptions, lead times, and substitution limits in one worksheet; a low price without availability is unusable.
Use USAspending.gov to frame incumbent and buying-pattern questions, then verify current requirements in the live solicitation rather than extrapolating eligibility.
Sell a paid bid/no-bid assessment before a large proposal engagement; documenting a defensible decision to decline can be the customer's highest-value outcome.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Deliver Three Reviewable Packets Without Becoming a Paper Prime
paragraphs: The third week tests whether the desk can turn public requirements into accepted customer work without creating new procurement risk. By Day 21, assemble three reviewable packets across the paid assignments: a qualification assessment, an amendment-controlled calendar, and a supplier or teaming worksheet. Each packet must be a separately identified contractual deliverable or milestone; splitting one document into three files does not satisfy the target. A completed bid submission is optional because the government's timetable may not fit the launch month. The customer remains the bidder and approves representations, pricing, signatures, and final submission. Use the agency's designated portal, including PIEE solicitation functionality where instructed, or the city's published bidding system. Do not share customer passwords; use authorized delegated access when available and retain the submission receipt. Measure delivery reliability against the customer-approved internal deadline, ideally one business day ahead of the official deadline. A proposal that misses the official cutoff cannot be rescued by a beautiful internal checklist. Compare attachments, file limits, required acknowledgments, and signature authority with the current instructions immediately before release. Treat a late amendment as a fresh review event, not an informal email addendum.

P5 supplier diligence establishes whether quoted performance is real: verify legal entity, actual capacity, reference contacts, delivery geography, insurance when required, and quote validity. For federal opportunities, inspect applicable exclusion records and relevant solicitation clauses rather than declaring every vendor eligible from a single search. P6 teaming assistance then documents the actual division of work, pricing responsibilities, customer ownership, and subcontract administration. FAR Subpart 9.6 recognizes contractor team arrangements, but it does not eliminate responsibility, competition, or small-business requirements. Apply 13 CFR 125.6 when limitations on subcontracting govern the particular set-aside or contract; identify the contract category, applicable payment base, and treatment of similarly situated entities before calculating any percentage. Evaluate ostensible-subcontractor concerns under 13 CFR 121.103(h), including who performs primary and vital requirements and whether the prime is unusually reliant on another business. Where applicable, FAR 52.215-23 restricts excessive pass-through charges when the contractor adds no or negligible value. A nominal prime that merely forwards invoices is not the same business as a fee-based bid-support desk. Escalate ambiguous structures to the retained specialist before pricing or introducing counterparties, and reject structures that cannot meet the applicable requirements.

Create a review ledger with two distinct measures. Mandatory-control completion must equal 100%: eligibility checks, required signatures, deadline verification, amendment acknowledgment, and authorized release cannot be averaged away. Separately require at least 95% first-pass accuracy across all checklist fields; calculate correct fields divided by inspected fields and keep the denominator. Review every packet during the pilot rather than drawing a small sample. Record defects by source, consequence, repair time, and responsible play. A missed attachment points to P4; an expired supplier quote points to P5; a missed date points to P3. P7 closes the loop with customer acceptance, earned-fee evidence, an invoice, and a scheduled collection follow-up. Government payment timing does not automatically determine when a private customer owes the desk; the service agreement controls that relationship. Do not describe the federal Prompt Payment Act as a direct remedy for every private consulting invoice. Track open invoices by contractual due date and dispute reason. If a customer insists on paying only after award, exclude that engagement from the early-cash test and review its compensation structure. The 6–18-month first-deal horizon makes award-dependent working capital especially dangerous for this five-person operating pod.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30 and Beyond: Apply Kill / Fix / Scale to Evidence, Not Optimism
paragraphs: Use the final nine days to audit the experiment rather than manufacture a dramatic award announcement. Reconcile the bank ledger, service orders, accepted milestones, timesheets, invoices, and source-linked opportunity records. Count only unrelated paying customer businesses, excluding founder transfers, barter, refundable demonstrations, and uncollected promises. Day 30's commercial Scale threshold is 40 qualified accounts contacted, eight completed discoveries, three priced proposals, two paying customers, $4,000 cumulative collected service fees, and three accepted packets. This is permission to repeat a controlled experiment, not to forecast a procurement award. Operational Scale also requires at least 60% realized contribution on completed work, 100% mandatory controls, at least 95% first-pass field accuracy, all customer milestones on time, and the required cash reserve. Calculate contribution using earned service revenue less direct delivery labor and direct specialist costs, without deducting those costs twice in the operating ledger. A single strong customer cannot compensate for unresolved improper conduct. Stop the affected activity immediately if evidence shows an unlawful payment or unauthorized use of procurement information. Preserve the records and obtain specialist direction before deciding whether the broader service can continue in a corrected form.

Apply the decision hierarchy consistently at Days 30, 60, and 90: hard stops first, commercial Kill thresholds second, every Scale condition third, and Fix for remaining cases. The matrix states cumulative commercial targets and minimum paid evidence at each checkpoint. Falling below a Kill floor after completing the required outreach retires the tested offer-and-segment combination, not necessarily the entire company. Incomplete outreach means the experiment is unproven; allow one ten-business-day Fix cycle with a named owner and no increased spending cap. A second missed execution commitment retires that experiment. Day 60 Scale adds at least one paid repeat engagement; Day 90 requires at least three and removes dependence on a single lucky sale. From Day 60, require weighted average days outstanding of open invoices no greater than 45 and no undisputed invoice more than 60 days past its contractual due date. Weight invoice age by outstanding balance; use zero when no invoices remain open. For Scale, add at most 25% more committed delivery hours per checkpoint without exceeding 70 weekly hours. Hiring beyond the original pod requires a separate cash and workload case; checkpoint success alone does not authorize the Scaled seven-person configuration.

Reconcile the operating experiment to the annual scorecard before presenting results. Conservative recognized service revenue is $120,000, with $102,000 total costs and $18,000 owner net profit at 15%; Base is $560,000, $434,000 costs, and $126,000 profit at 22.5%; Scaled is $1,000,000, $700,000 costs, and $300,000 profit at 30%. Conservative and Base retain 2 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 3 FT + 4 C. Average monthly revenue equivalents are $10,000, approximately $46,667, and approximately $83,333, respectively, not first-month sales promises. The $20,000 launch outflow ceiling cannot be repeated all year inside Conservative's $102,000 annual cost envelope. A dedicated five-person delivery model may fail that scenario's labor economics; show the gap explicitly rather than erasing wages or changing the canonical profit. The launch cap is a cash stress limit, not a replacement annual expense forecast. Likewise, 60% package contribution must still absorb sales time, shared payroll, insurance, software, and other overhead before owner profit. Keep service revenue, customer award value, deposits, receivables, and owner distributions in separate ledger categories. At every checkpoint, compare actual cash consumption with remaining runway and stop new commitments before the protected reserve is consumed.

chapters.pull_quote: Scale the desk when customers pay for repeatable work, not when a government notice displays a large contract ceiling.
action_checklist: By Day 2, map P1–P7 into one source-linked register covering one supplier category, two federal buying offices, and one municipal portal.
By Day 5, validate the 2 FT + 3 C pod against actual rates, $90,000 available launch capital, and the $20,000 maximum monthly cash outflow.
By Day 14, issue three bounded proposals, secure the first paid assessment, and preserve separate records for cash deposits and earned service fees.

At Days 60 and 90, require paid repeat demand, acceptable receivables, protected runway, and canonical annual-cost reconciliation before increasing delivery commitments.
